Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 1–6:

Explanation of the words:

Alif-Lam-Mim (الۤمۤ): The discussion of its like has already occurred in Surah al-Baqarah, so refer to it there.

Allah: The One truly worthy of worship.

There is no god but He (لا إله إلا هو): There is no one truly worthy of worship besides Him.

Al-Hayy (الحيّ): The Possessor of life, which necessarily entails will, knowledge, hearing, sight and power.

Al-Qayyum (القيّوم): The One who sustains and watches over all His creatures through nurturing, care and preservation.

Al-Kitab (الكتاب): The Qur'an.

Bil-haqq (بالحق): Accompanied by truth, since everything in it is true and genuine, with no falsehood in it in any way whatsoever.

Musaddiqan limā bayna yadayh (مصدقاً لما بين يديه): Confirming the earlier scriptures, not contradicting or nullifying them, because the source of all of them is one: Allah, exalted is He.

At-Tawrah (التوراة): The Book of Musa, peace be upon him, and its meaning in Hebrew is "the Law" (al-shari'ah).

Al-Injil (الإنجيل): The Book of Isa, peace be upon him, and its meaning in Greek is "the new teaching" (al-ta'lim al-jadid).

Al-Furqan (الفرقان): That by which Allah distinguishes between truth and falsehood: the Qur'anic proofs, the divine miracles, and the clear human intellects that have not been overcome by blind imitation, rigidity and desire.

Yusawwiruku-m fi al-arham (يصوركم في الأرحام): Tasweer (تصوير) is bringing into being a form for a thing that did not previously have it. Al-arham is the plural of rahm (رحم), the place where the fetus is lodged.

Meaning of the verses:

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari related with sound chains of narration that the delegation of Najran, numbering sixty riders, including their nobles and the people who bind and loose affairs among them, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to dispute with him concerning the matter of the Messiah, peace be upon him, wishing to establish his divinity through false claims. Allah then revealed more than eighty verses from the opening of this surah, from Alif-Lam-Mim up to nearly eighty, as a refutation of their falsehood and an establishment of proof against them. The one who reflects on these verses will notice this and see it clearly and manifestly in the Qur'anic context of these verses.

Allah, exalted is He, said: Alif-Lam-Mim. Allah, there is no god but He. He informed that none is truly worthy of worship except Him, thereby nullifying the worship of the Messiah, peace be upon him, and the worship of every object of worship other than Allah, exalted is He, among all other objects of worship. He said: The Living, the Self-Subsisting. He mentioned the proof that He alone deserves worship, which is that He, exalted is He, is Living from eternity to eternity, while every other living being is preceded by non-existence and is subject to annihilation. Therefore none deserves divinity except Him, Mighty and Majestic. The Messiah, peace be upon him, was preceded by non-existence and is subject to annihilation, so how could he be a god? He said: Al-Qayyum, that is, the One who sustains all creation through nurturing, care, preservation, management and provision. Anything other than Him does not have this quality; rather it is nurtured and provided for. So how could it be a god alongside Allah? The evidence for this is that He has sent down to you the Book, the Qur'an, accompanied by truth, containing nothing of falsehood. Its verses all affirm the divinity of Allah and negate it from anything else. So how could the Messiah be a god alongside Allah, or be Allah Himself, or the son of Allah, as the Christians of Najran and others claim, and as the Christians of Greece, Rome and elsewhere claim? He sent it down confirming what came before it of the books that preceded it, not opposing them and not contradicting them. This shows that it is the revelation of Allah. He sent down the Tawrah and the Injil before it as guidance for mankind, and He sent down the Furqan, by which He distinguished between truth and falsehood in every matter that is confused for people. It became clear that the Lord, the Creator, the Provider, the Manager of life, the Giver of life and the Causer of death, the Living who does not die, is the true God, and that whatever else is other than Him is a created nurtured being with no right to divinity or worship, even if it heals a sick person, makes a mute speak, or revives a dead person by the permission of Allah, exalted is He. That does not qualify it to be a god alongside Allah, as with Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him. What he did of healing the blind and the leper and reviving some of the dead was by the power of Allah and His permission granted to Isa; otherwise he would not have been able to do any of that, his situation being like that of every servant of Allah, exalted is He. When the delegation rejected what the Messenger had argued with them and the proof he had established against them, their disbelief was confirmed, and the Lord, exalted is He, threatened them with His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Mighty, Owner of Retribution﴾. This is a severe threat against everyone who denies the signs of Allah and rejects the truth that they carry concerning the Oneness of Allah, exalted is He, and the obligation to obey Him and to obey His Messenger ﷺ. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾. So if there were anyone who deserved divinity alongside Him, He would know of him and would have reported him. Through this statement He also affirmed that His might cannot be challenged and that He is certainly capable of exacting retribution from the people of disbelief in Him.

He mentioned another proof for the invalidity of the divinity of the Messiah, saying: ﴿He it is who forms you in the wombs however He wills﴾. Isa, peace be upon him, was formed in the womb of Maryam, so he is certainly among those whom Allah formed. How then could he be a god alongside Allah, or a son of Allah, as the Christians claim? Here He established the reality, saying: ﴿There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. The might that cannot be challenged and the wisdom that does not err are the requirements of His true divinity, which none disputes except the arrogant and none denies except the obstinate, such as the delegation of the Christians of Najran and those of their kind among the people of disbelief and obstinacy.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the divinity of Allah, exalted is He, through proofs, and the negation of divinity from anyone else among all His creatures.

2- Confirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ through Allah's sending down the Book to him.

3- Allah establishes His proof upon His servants by sending down His books and the Furqan within them, clarifying truth and falsehood in all matters of life.

4- The invalidity of the divinity of the Messiah, since he is a created being formed in the wombs like others, whom Allah formed as He willed. How then could he be a god alongside Allah or a son of His, exalted is Allah above that by a great exaltation?

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari related with sound chains of narration that the delegation of Najran, numbering sixty riders, including their nobles and the people who bind and loose affairs among them, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to dispute with him concerning the matter of the Messiah, peace be upon him, wishing to establish his divinity through false claims. Allah then revealed more than eighty verses from the opening of this surah, from Alif-Lam-Mim up to nearly eighty, as a refutation of their falsehood and an establishment of proof against them. The one who reflects on these verses will notice this and see it clearly and manifestly in the Qur'anic context of these verses.

Allah, exalted is He, said: Alif-Lam-Mim. Allah, there is no god but He. He informed that none is truly worthy of worship except Him, thereby nullifying the worship of the Messiah, peace be upon him, and the worship of every object of worship other than Allah, exalted is He, among all other objects of worship. He said: The Living, the Self-Subsisting. He mentioned the proof that He alone deserves worship, which is that He, exalted is He, is Living from eternity to eternity, while every other living being is preceded by non-existence and is subject to annihilation. Therefore none deserves divinity except Him, Mighty and Majestic. The Messiah, peace be upon him, was preceded by non-existence and is subject to annihilation, so how could he be a god? He said: Al-Qayyum, that is, the One who sustains all creation through nurturing, care, preservation, management and provision. Anything other than Him does not have this quality; rather it is nurtured and provided for. So how could it be a god alongside Allah? The evidence for this is that He has sent down to you the Book, the Qur'an, accompanied by truth, containing nothing of falsehood. Its verses all affirm the divinity of Allah and negate it from anything else. So how could the Messiah be a god alongside Allah, or be Allah Himself, or the son of Allah, as the Christians of Najran and others claim, and as the Christians of Greece, Rome and elsewhere claim? He sent it down confirming what came before it of the books that preceded it, not opposing them and not contradicting them. This shows that it is the revelation of Allah. He sent down the Tawrah and the Injil before it as guidance for mankind, and He sent down the Furqan, by which He distinguished between truth and falsehood in every matter that is confused for people. It became clear that the Lord, the Creator, the Provider, the Manager of life, the Giver of life and the Causer of death, the Living who does not die, is the true God, and that whatever else is other than Him is a created nurtured being with no right to divinity or worship, even if it heals a sick person, makes a mute speak, or revives a dead person by the permission of Allah, exalted is He. That does not qualify it to be a god alongside Allah, as with Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him. What he did of healing the blind and the leper and reviving some of the dead was by the power of Allah and His permission granted to Isa; otherwise he would not have been able to do any of that, his situation being like that of every servant of Allah, exalted is He. When the delegation rejected what the Messenger had argued with them and the proof he had established against them, their disbelief was confirmed, and the Lord, exalted is He, threatened them with His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Mighty, Owner of Retribution﴾. This is a severe threat against everyone who denies the signs of Allah and rejects the truth that they carry concerning the Oneness of Allah, exalted is He, and the obligation to obey Him and to obey His Messenger ﷺ. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾. So if there were anyone who deserved divinity alongside Him, He would know of him and would have reported him. Through this statement He also affirmed that His might cannot be challenged and that He is certainly capable of exacting retribution from the people of disbelief in Him.

He mentioned another proof for the invalidity of the divinity of the Messiah, saying: ﴿He it is who forms you in the wombs however He wills﴾. Isa, peace be upon him, was formed in the womb of Maryam, so he is certainly among those whom Allah formed. How then could he be a god alongside Allah, or a son of Allah, as the Christians claim? Here He established the reality, saying: ﴿There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. The might that cannot be challenged and the wisdom that does not err are the requirements of His true divinity, which none disputes except the arrogant and none denies except the obstinate, such as the delegation of the Christians of Najran and those of their kind among the people of disbelief and obstinacy.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the divinity of Allah, exalted is He, through proofs, and the negation of divinity from anyone else among all His creatures.

2- Confirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ through Allah's sending down the Book to him.

3- Allah establishes His proof upon His servants by sending down His books and the Furqan within them, clarifying truth and falsehood in all matters of life.

4- The invalidity of the divinity of the Messiah, since he is a created being formed in the wombs like others, whom Allah formed as He willed. How then could he be a god alongside Allah or a son of His, exalted is Allah above that by a great exaltation?

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verse 7–9:

Explanation of the words:

Muhkamat (the clear ones): those whose meaning is apparent and manifest, admitting of only one meaning. These are such as the verses of legal rulings concerning the lawful and the unlawful, the prescribed limits (hudud), acts of worship, and lessons and admonitions.

Mutashabihat (the ambiguous ones): those whose meaning is not apparent, admitting of several meanings, such that it is difficult for anyone other than those firmly rooted in knowledge to speak about them. They include the opening letters of the surahs and matters of the unseen. Like the saying of Allah the Exalted concerning Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿...and His word which He directed to Mary and a spirit from Him...﴾ [An-Nisa: 171], and His saying the Exalted: ﴿...The decision is only for Allah...﴾ [Al-An'am: 57].

In their hearts is deviation (zaygh): zaygh is inclining away from the truth due to a doubt, a desire, or a trial.

Seeking discord (ibtigha' al-fitnah): that is, seeking to cause the believers to fall into trouble regarding their religion and their beliefs.

Seeking its interpretation (ibtigha' ta'wilihi): seeking its interpretation so that it agrees with their corrupt beliefs.

And none knows its interpretation except Allah: and none knows what the matter of the ambiguous verses will ultimately come to except Allah, who sent it down.

Those firmly rooted in knowledge (al-rasikhun fi al-'ilm): they are the people of certain knowledge in their souls, whose feet are firmly planted in knowing the truth, so they do not slip and do not exceed bounds into doubt or falsehood.

Each is from our Lord: that is, the clear and the ambiguous alike; so we believe in all of it.

Men of understanding (ulu al-albab): possessors of sound intellects and upright comprehension.

Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate: that is, do not turn our hearts away from the truth after You have guided us to it and made us know it, so that we know it.

Grant us from Yourself: give us mercy from Your presence.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted continues to establish His lordship, His divinity, and the prophethood of His Messenger, and refutes the claim of the Christians of Najran regarding the divinity of the Messiah, peace be upon him. He says: He, Allah, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, is the One who sent down to you the Book, meaning the Qur'an. In it are clear verses (muhkamat), in which there is no abrogation and no obscurity in their meaning or in their indication of what they were revealed for; and these are the majority of the verses of the Book, and they are its mother and its origin. And in it are other verses (mutashabihat), and these are few. The wisdom in sending them down is a test and an examination, like the examination by the lawful and the unlawful, and by matters of the unseen, so that whoever Allah wills to guide remains steadfast in guidance and faith, and whoever Allah wills to be led astray and not guided is made to deviate in his faith and to stray from His path. So the Exalted said: ﴿As for those in whose hearts is deviation...﴾, meaning inclination away from the truth, ﴿they follow what is ambiguous of it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation﴾, to turn people away from the path of truth and the guidance of creation, as the Christians did when they claimed that Allah is the third of three, because He says: "We create and give life, and cause death." This is the statement of a group or more. And as they said regarding His saying about Jesus: ﴿...and a spirit from Him...﴾ [An-Nisa: 171], that he is a part of Him united with Him. And as the Kharijites said regarding His saying the Exalted: ﴿...The decision is only for Allah...﴾ [Al-An'am: 57], that no one may judge in anything, and they declared 'Ali to be a disbeliever and departed from him because he appointed Abu Musa al-Ash'ari as arbiter in the essence of the dispute between 'Ali and Mu'awiyah. Thus do the people of deviation fall into error, for they follow the ambiguous and do not refer it back to the clear, whereby its meaning would become evident to them and they would understand Allah's intended meaning from it. And He, the Exalted, informs that none knows its interpretation except Him, glorified and exalted be He.

And that those firmly rooted in knowledge entrust its matter to Allah who sent it down, so they say: ﴿...We believe in it; all is from our Lord. And none will be reminded except the people of understanding.﴾ They ask their Lord for steadfastness upon the truth, saying: ﴿...Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy...﴾, by which You show us mercy in our worldly life and our Hereafter; indeed You alone are the Bestower, there is no god besides You and no lord other than You. They also affirm the principle of resurrection and the Hereafter, saying, supplicating and humbly beseeching: ﴿Our Lord, indeed You are the gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾, to account for them and recompense them for their deeds. So forgive us and have mercy on us that Day, since we believed in You, Your Messenger, and Your Book, its clear verses and its ambiguous ones. Indeed, You do not fail in the promise.

Guidance from the verses:

1- In the Book of Allah there are the clear and the ambiguous. The clear must be believed in and acted upon according to its requirements, and the ambiguous must be believed in and its interpretation entrusted to Allah who sent it down, and it is said: ﴿...We believe in it; all is from our Lord...﴾.

2- The people of deviation who follow what is ambiguous must be shunned and turned away from, for they are innovators and people of desires.

3- Recommendation of supplicating for salvation when deviation appears and when trials and error are seen.

4- Affirmation of the principle of the resurrection and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 10–13:

Explanation of the words:

Inna alladhina kafaru (Indeed, those who disbelieve): they are the delegation of Najran, the Jews of Madinah, the polytheists and the hypocrites.

Lan tughni 'anhum (will not avail them): will not ransom them, nor protect them from the punishment of God when it descends upon them.

Waqud al-nar (fuel of the Fire): al-waqud is that with which fire is kindled, such as firewood, coal or gas.

Ka-da'b Al Fir'awn (like the custom of the family of Pharaoh): like their habit and practice in their disbelief and denial, and the punishment that befell them in this world and the Hereafter.

Qul lilladhina kafaru (Say to those who disbelieve): they are the Jews of Madinah, the Banu Qaynuqa'.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verse 14:

Explanation of the words:

"Zuyyina li'n-nasi hubb ash-shahawat" (He made appealing to people the love of desires): He made their love seem pleasing in their souls, so that they see in it no ugliness or repulsiveness.

Ash-shahawat (desires): the plural of shahwah (desire), meaning what is naturally and instinctively desired, such as delicious food and drink.

Al-qanatir al-muqantarah (heaped-up hoards of gold and silver): al-qintar is one thousand and one hundred ounces of silver, and al-muqantarah means much of it, piled one upon another.

Al-khayl al-musawwamah (branded horses): those with fine markings, prepared for riding in raids and jihad.

Al-an'am (livestock): camels, cattle and sheep, which are the grazing animals.

Al-harth (tilled land): the crops, fields and all beneficial plants.

"Dhalika mata' al-hayat ad-dunya" (That is the enjoyment of the worldly life): that is, what has been mentioned of women, sons, etc. is the enjoyment of the worldly life; one enjoys it in this world, and its owner dies and leaves it.

Meaning of the noble verse:

When the Exalted mentioned the obstinacy of those who disbelieved, from the Christians, the Jews and the polytheists, and their denial and disbelief, He mentioned the cause of disbelief and explained its reason, namely what the Exalted made appealing to humankind in general in order to test them and examine them with it: the love of desires, that is, the things desired by human nature, such as women, sons, heaped-up hoards of gold and silver, branded horses, livestock and tilled land, which is everything sown of grains, nutritional and aromatic plants and others. This is what caused those communities to reject the truth and repel it, because it generally stands between them and these desires, so they do not obtain them. They did not know that these are merely fleeting enjoyment, so they do not sell the Garden, the abode of eternity and peace, for them. That is why the Exalted said: "That," i.e. what has been mentioned of the categories of beloved things, "is the enjoyment of the worldly life," and nothing more. As for the Hereafter, none of that benefits there; rather, nothing benefits there except renunciation of it and turning away from it, except what is necessary for sustenance toward the work of the Hereafter, which is faith and righteous deeds, and abandoning disbelief, polytheism and all sins and disobedience.

The Exalted concluded the verse by encouraging work for the Hereafter and calling His servants to renounce the perishing enjoyment, so that their hearts become attached to the lasting bliss, saying: "And with Allah is the best return" (﴿وٱللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ ٱلْمَآبِ﴾), i.e. the good return, the noble abode, and the good and happy dwelling.

Guidance from the verse:

1- "Yuzayyin Allah" means that God makes a thing an object of love for people as a trial and test. The Exalted said: "Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed" (﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا ما عَلى ٱلأَرْضِ زِينَةً لَّها لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ أيُّهُم أحْسَنُ عَمَلاً﴾ [Al-Kahf: 7]). And Satan makes things appealing for misguidance and seduction. So Allah makes beauty beautiful and makes ugliness ugly, while Satan makes ugliness appealing and makes beauty repulsive. So observe the difference and reflect.

2- The adornments mentioned in this verse are from Allah's making them appealing as a trial, and all of them are in reality adornments, and there is nothing ugly in them, except when they are sought from other than their lawful source and taken with greed and avidity, so they corrupt the character of the one who takes them, or love for them overpowers him, making him forget the meeting with Allah and what is with Him, so he perishes through them, like the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists.

3- Everything in this world is merely enjoyment, and enjoyment is always little and fleeting, so the intelligent person should look at it as it is, and not pursue it in a way that deprives him of the good return with Allah. O Allah, do not deprive us of Your good return, O Allah, O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 3, verses 15–17:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*U'nabi'ukum* (أؤنبئكُمْ): I inform you of a great news, because *naba'* (news) is only used for a matter of great importance.

*Bi-khayrin min dhalikum* (بخير من ذلكم): that is, better than what was mentioned in the previous verse of women, sons, etc.

*Ittaqu* (اتقوا): fear their Lord, so that they abandon associating partners with Him and disobeying Him and His Messenger.

*Min tahtiha al-anhar* (من تحتها الأنهار): through its palaces and trees flow rivers of water, rivers of milk, rivers of honey and rivers of wine.

*Khalidina fiha abadan* (خالدين فيها أبدا): remaining therein in a state from which they will never depart again.

*Azwaj mutahhara* (أزواج مطهرة): wives who are the *hur al-'in* (lustrous-eyed maidens), pure from menstrual blood, urine, and every harm and impurity.

*As-sabirin* (الصابرين): patient in obedience, never abandoning it; patient in adversity, not showing discontent; and refraining from sins, not committing them.

*As-sadiqin* (الصادقين): truthful in their faith, their words and their deeds.

*Al-qanitin* (القانتين): worshippers who do good, who call upon Allah and humbly supplicate Him.

*Wal-munfiqin* (والمنفقين): those who pay *zakat* and give charity from the surplus of their wealth.

*Al-mustaghfirin bil-asḥar* (المستغفرين بالأسحار): those who ask their Lord for forgiveness in the last part of the night, at the time of *suhur*.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When the Exalted explained what He had made appealing to people, namely love of desires such as women, sons, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, and what else He mentioned, and showed that the best return is with Him, glory be to Him, so it should be sought from Him through faith and righteous deeds, He commanded His Messenger to say to all people: "Shall I inform you of something better than that which has been mentioned to you?" He explained it by His saying: ﴿For those who are mindful of Allah, with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally, and pure spouses, and approval from Allah﴾, and that is His good pleasure with them, which is greater than the bliss mentioned before it. He said in another verse: ﴿But approval from Allah is greater﴾ [at-Tawbah: 72].

Then He informed that He is Seeing of His servants, knowing the true believer and the hypocrite liar, the good doer and the evildoer, and He will recompense each by His justice and bounty. Then He mentioned the attributes of the God-fearing by which they inherited what was described of bliss, so He said: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾. He mentioned the attribute of faith, fear, humble supplication and their calling upon Him, then mentioned the remaining perfect attributes, saying: ﴿the patient, the truthful, the devoutly obedient, the spenders, and those who seek forgiveness before dawn﴾. They pray at the last part of the night and shortly before the break of dawn, and they frequently seek forgiveness, which is asking for pardon.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The bliss of the Hereafter is better than the bliss of this world, whatever it may be.
2. The bliss of the Hereafter is specific to the God-fearing righteous, while the bliss of this world is often for the wicked.
3. Taqwa, which is abandoning shirk and sins, is the means of inheriting the Abode of Peace.
4. Recommendation of humble supplication, calling upon Allah, and seeking forgiveness in the last part of the night.
5. The attributes mentioned here for the people of taqwa are all obligatory in general; it is not permissible for any believing man or woman to lack them in life.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 18–20:

Explanation of the words:

Shahida (bore witness): he informed, on the basis of knowledge of the matter he witnessed.

La ilaha illa Huwa (there is no god but He): there is no one worthy of worship in the earth or in the heavens except Allah, blessed and exalted.

Ulu al-'ilm (those possessed of knowledge): people of sound knowledge that corresponds to reality, namely the prophets and the scholars.

Al-qist (justice): justice in judgment, speech and action.

Al-'Aziz al-Hakim (the Mighty, the All-Wise): the Victorious, possessor of a might that cannot be overcome; the Wise in all His creation, His actions and all His dispositions.

Al-din (religion): that by which one submits to God Most High, that is, the laws and acts of worship by which He is obeyed and to which one submits.

Al-Islam (submission): submission to God through obedience and sincerity free from shirk; what is meant here is the religion of Islam.

Baghyan (out of insolence): out of injustice and envy.

Hajjuka (they argued with you): they disputed with you and contended against you with false and feeble proofs.

Aslamtu wajhiya lillah (I have submitted my face to Allah): I have devoted all my inner and outer deeds to Allah alone, without partner.

Wa-man ittaba'an (and whoever follows me): likewise, they have devoted all their deeds to Allah alone, without partner.

Utu al-kitab (those given the Book): the Jews and the Christians.

Al-ummiyyin (the unlettered): the pagan Arabs, so called because few among them could read or write.

A-aslamtum (Have you submitted?): the first hamza is interrogative, and what is meant is a command, i.e., submit, which is better for you, since the truth has become manifest and its light has shone forth among you through the books of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

Fa-in aslamu (then if they submit): if they answer you and submit, then they have been guided to the path of salvation.

Wa-in tawallaw (but if they turn away): they turn their backs on the truth after seeing it and turn away from it after knowing it; their affair does not harm you, since your duty is only to convey, and you have conveyed.

Meaning of the verses:

The Almighty, Majestic, informs that He bore witness that there is no god but He, and that the angels and those possessed of knowledge bear witness likewise, a witness of knowledge and truth founded on the principle of essential and actual presence, and that He, exalted is He, stands over all the dominion, the high and the low, with justice. There is no lord other than Him and no god besides Him, the Mighty in His dominion and creation, the Wise in His governance and disposition, so He never places anything other than in its fitting place. By this testimony He refuted the falsehood of the Christians of Najran, the deceit of the Jews, and the polytheism of the Arabs, and He nullified all their falsehood, glory be to Him and exalted is He. Then He also informed that the true religion, which He accepts no other from, is Islam, founded on the principle of complete submission to Allah Most High in obedience and total sincerity free from all kinds of shirk. So He said: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾, meaning that in His judgment and decree the religion is Islam, and whatever else is other than it He does not accept or approve. Then Most High informed of the state of the Christians of Najran, who argued with His Messenger, concerning their deifying of Jesus falsely, so He said: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of insolence among themselves﴾. He means that the disagreement of the People of the Book was not from ignorance of the truth or lack of knowing it, but was from genuine knowledge; what drove them to the disagreement that causes strife, wars and the loss of religion was insolence and envy, since each sect wants leadership and religious and worldly authority for itself alone, and thereby both religion and worldly life are corrupted. This is a human custom into which the Muslims also fell after the preferred generations, and history is witness.

Then He, Most High, said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. He threatens and warns every one who disbelieves in His signs that carry His laws, denying them and turning away from them, that He Most High counts against him the sins of his disbelief and the evils of his disobedience, calls him to account and recompenses him, and that He is indeed swift in reckoning, because nothing preoccupies Him from another, and counting and number do not weary Him. Then He turns the address to His Messenger, saying to him: "And if they argue with you," meaning the Christian delegation of Najran. So conclude the disputation with them by displaying your position, which disheartens them, inviting them to Islam, which they recognize and deny out of concern for leadership and interests among themselves. So say to them: ﴿I have submitted my face to Allah, and so have those who follow me﴾, that is, likewise they have submitted their faces to Allah; there is nothing in us for other than Allah, and our hearts, deeds and lives are all for Allah. So submit, you People of the Book and you unlettered ones. ﴿Then if they submit, they are guided﴾. And if they turn away and refuse, their refusal does not harm you, since you were only charged with conveying, and you have conveyed. As for the reckoning and recompense, it belongs to Allah Most High, the Seer of the deeds of His servants, the Knower of their intentions; He will recompense them by His knowledge and judge among them by His wisdom, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The recognition of testimony and acting upon it, if it is founded on knowledge and the witness is qualified for that, being a Muslim and upright.

2- The testimony of Allah is the greatest testimony by which laws and rulings are established, followed by the testimony of the angels and those possessed of knowledge.

3- The invalidity of every religion after Islam and every creed other than its creed, because of Allah Most High's testimony to that and His saying: ﴿...And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter﴾, verse [85] of this surah, whose explanation will follow, Allah willing.

4- Disagreement among the people of knowledge and religion occurs when they prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter, becoming entangled in food and drink, longing for seats and positions, and desiring honor; then on that day they differ out of insolence among themselves and envy of one another.

5- Whoever submits his heart to Allah and his limbs, and becomes devoted in his life to Allah, has been guided to the path of salvation and peace.

6- Whoever attaches his heart to the life of this world and turns away from what would divert him from it, in acts of worship, has gone astray in his life and his striving, and his reckoning is with Allah, and he will meet his recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 21–22:

Explanation of the words:

Yakfurūn (يكفرون): they deny and reject.

Al-nabiyyīn (النبيين): plural of nabi (prophet), a male descendant of Adam to whom Allah revealed.

Al-qist (القسط): justice, truth, goodness and what is right.

Bashshirhum bi-adhābin alīm (بشرهم بعذاب أليم): inform them in a way whose effect shows on the skin of their faces as pain and grief.

Ḥabiṭat a'māluhum (حبِطت أعمالهم): were nullified and gone; they gain nothing from them that benefits them. They are destroyed by that, and have no helper, because Allah has forsaken them and intended their destruction and their punishment in Hell.

The meaning of the two verses:

The context still continues to expose the deeds of the unbelievers among the People of the Two Scriptures, the Jews and the Christians. Here Allah the Exalted mentions that those who deny the signs of Allah, which are His proofs and the markers of His religion, and with which His messengers were sent, and who, in addition, kill the prophets without right and without any justification for killing, and kill those among the followers of the prophets, the believing righteous, who command them to justice, these are the crimes of some of the People of the Book. So give them the good news of a painful punishment. Then He informs that those far removed in the abysses of evil, corruption, injustice and obstinacy, their deeds are nullified in this world, so they gain from them no good outcome and no praise or commendation; rather, curses are recorded against them for them in life and in death, and likewise in the Hereafter, and they have no helpers who could rescue them from the punishment of Allah. Far, far is it that anyone besides Allah could be found as a guardian or a helper.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Disbelief and injustice are causes of destruction in this world and of the obligation of punishment in the Hereafter.

2- Killing those who command what is right and forbid what is wrong is like the killing of the prophets in the enormity of the crime.

3- Shirk nullifies deeds and corrupts them in this world and the Hereafter.

4- Whom Allah forsakes, no one helps; and whom Allah helps, no one overcomes.

Here Allah the Exalted mentions that those who deny the signs of Allah, which are His proofs and the markers of His religion, and with which His messengers were sent, and who, in addition, kill the prophets without right and without any justification for killing, and kill those among the followers of the prophets, the believing righteous, who command them to justice, these are the crimes of some of the People of the Book. So give them the good news of a painful punishment. Then He informs that those far removed in the abysses of evil, corruption, injustice and obstinacy, their deeds are nullified in this world, so they gain from them no good outcome and no praise or commendation; rather, curses are recorded against them for them in life and in death, and likewise in the Hereafter, and they have no helpers who could rescue them from the punishment of Allah. Far, far is it that anyone besides Allah could be found as a guardian or a helper.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Disbelief and injustice are causes of destruction in this world and of the obligation of punishment in the Hereafter.

2- Killing those who command what is right and forbid what is wrong is like the killing of the prophets in the enormity of the crime.

3- Shirk nullifies deeds and corrupts them in this world and the Hereafter.

4- Whom Allah forsakes, no one helps; and whom Allah helps, no one overcomes.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 23–25:

Explanation of the words:

"Given a portion of the Scripture" (أوتوا نصيباً من الكتاب): they were given a share and a portion of the Torah (al-Tawrah).

"They are called" (يدعون): they are asked to submit their disputes over the truth to their Book, in which they believe, which is the Torah, but they refuse and turn away.

"Turns away" (يتولى): he returns while being determined not to come back to the truth.

"Numbered days" (أياما معدودات): this is the saying of the Jews, and by the days they mean forty days, the period in which they worshipped the calf after Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, had been absent from them.

"They invent" (يفترون): they lie.

"A Day about which there is no doubt" (ليوم لا ريب فيه): this is the Day of Resurrection.

"What they earned" (ما كسبت): what they did of good or evil.

"They will not be wronged" (لا يظلمون): by being punished without a cause that warrants their punishment, such as polytheism, disbelief and sins.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to expose the People of the Book by mentioning their sins and crimes. Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger, prompting him to wonder at the condition of the Jews: "﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾" That is, has not your knowledge reached their situation, when they are called to submit to the Book of Allah the Exalted concerning what they denied and disputed regarding your attributes and the matter of your prophethood and messengership? Then a group of them turn away, being determined not to return to seeking the truth and acknowledging it. This is truly a condition that calls for wonder, and what diverts them from accepting the truth and returning to it is their corrupt belief that the Fire will not touch them if they are thrown into it except for a period of forty days, the period in which their forefathers worshipped the calf when Musa was absent from them while he communed with his Lord on Mount Tur. This claim is false and has no basis in truth. Rather, they will abide in the Fire not because their forefathers worshipped the calf for forty days, but because of their disbelief, their wrongdoing, their denial and their obstinacy. Allah the Exalted clarifies the reality to His Messenger and the believers: this Jewish claim is nothing but a fabrication that their scholars invented in order to make it easy for them to commit crimes and fall into great sins, just as occurred among Muslims in the dark ages of Islamic history, when the shaykhs of Sufism deceived their disciples by claiming that they would intercede for them and that they would be forgiven.

How will their condition be? It is a condition that description cannot capture. "﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it earned﴾" of good or evil, "﴿and they will not be wronged﴾" by having their good deeds diminished, if they had any good deeds, nor by an increase in their evil deeds, for they have nothing but evil deeds.

1- Among the forms of turning away from religion and rejecting it is refusing to submit to its judgment. Allah the Exalted says: "﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely.﴾" [An-Nisa: 65].

2- Among the most harmful things to religions, in their beliefs, laws and worship, is fabrication about them, innovation in them, and speaking about them without knowledge.

3- The harm of being deceived by what some exegetes and annotators of religious books say, namely stories and falsehoods, under the pretext of encouragement or warning, so that people are deceived, go astray and perish.

4- The virtue of mentioning the horrors of the Day of Resurrection and what the people of injustice, evil and corruption will encounter therein. In the Qur'an: "﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure [quality]: the remembrance of the Home [of the Hereafter]﴾" [Sad: 46].

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 3, verses 26–27**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Allāhumma* (O Allah): This is "yā Allāh" with the particle of calling "yā" omitted and the doubled letter "mīm" put in its place; it is specific to calling upon Allah, the Exalted.

*Mālik* (Sovereign): The *mālik* is the ruler who disposes of the dominion, doing with it whatever He wills and judging as He desires, due to the greatness of His authority and the strength of His will.

*al-Mulk* (dominion): The *mamlūk* (that which is owned). What is meant is everything other than the Owner, Mighty and Majestic, of all created beings.

*Tu'tī al-mulk* (You give dominion): Authority and disposal over some part of the realm of dominion (*malakūt*).

*Tūlij al-layl fī al-nahār* (You cause the night to enter into the day): You make the night enter into the day so that no night remains, and You make the day enter into the night so that no day remains.

*Tukhrij al-ḥayy min al-mayyit* (You bring the living out of the dead): That is, You bring a living body out of a dead body in tangible things, such as the chick from the egg and the egg from the chicken; and in non-physical matters, You bring the believer out of the disbeliever and the disbeliever out of the believer.

*Bi-ghayr ḥisāb* (without reckoning): Without number or limit, because of His vast bounty and His self-sufficiency from all else.

**The meaning of the two verses:**

Among the occasions said to have been the reason for the revelation of these two verses: when the Messenger ﷺ informed his companions, in sound narrations, that the dominion of his community would reach such-and-such extent, the Jews and the hypocrites mocked the Messenger's report, deeming it extremely far-fetched, out of their ignorance and disbelief. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed these two verses within a response to the Christians of Najran, commanding him to say: ﴿O Allah, Sovereign of dominion, You give dominion to whom You will...﴾ etc. He was commanded to say this in order to grant him what He had promised him of the expansion of his community's dominion, so that it would encompass the realms of Persia and Byzantium, and to refute the error of the Christians in deifying Jesus, peace be upon him. For the one truly worthy of worship and deification, deserving it to the exclusion of all others, is the One who owns the whole dominion and disposes of it alone; He gives of it what He wills to whom He wills, and He removes it from those to whom He gave it whenever He wills; no barrier prevents His disposal, and no one who stands can stop His giving or taking away. He honors the humiliated whenever He wills and humbles the honored whenever He wills. In His hand is good, not in the hand of another; He pours it upon whom He wills and withholds it from whom He wills, and He is over all things Capable. He causes the day to enter into the night so that no day remains, and He causes the night to enter into the day so that no night remains: a manifestation of the power that necessitates His divinity, obedience to Him, and love for Him. He causes hours of the night to enter into the day, so the night becomes shorter and the day longer, and He causes hours of the day to enter into the night, so it becomes longer: a manifestation of wisdom, power, and mercy. He brings the living out of the dead: man from the sperm-drop, and the plant from the seed; and He brings the dead out of the living: the sperm-drop from the living man, the egg from the hen, and the disbelieving dead from the believing living, and the reverse likewise. These are manifestations of His Lordship, which entail His divinity. Thus it is established that He is the true God; there is no Lord other than Him and no god besides Him. By this two matters are confirmed. First: Allah is capable of granting His Messenger what He promised to his community, and He has done so. Second: Jesus was none other than a servant created and sustained by Allah, whom He honored with prophethood and supported with miracles.

**Guidance from the two verses:**

1. The virtue of supplicating with these two verses: the servant recites them, then says: (O Merciful of this world and the Hereafter, and its Merciful: You give from them to whom You will, and withhold from whom You will, settle my debt for me). He will, by Allah's permission, have his debt settled and be granted whatever he asks of the needs of this world and the Hereafter.

2. Allah's response to His Messenger ﷺ and His fulfilment of what He promised concerning his community.

3. The invalidity of the divinity of Jesus, peace be upon him, and the affirmation of his servanthood, prophethood, and honor.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 28–30:

Explanation of the words:

Yattakhidh (take): yaj'al (make, consider).

Awliya' (allies, protectors): plural of wali, those whom one supports, loves and aids.

Fa-laysa min Allahi fi shay' (then he has nothing whatsoever to do with Allah): i.e., Allah is free of him, and whoever Allah disowns is ruined.

Tuqatan (taqiyyah, prudent self-protection): protection by the tongue, which is a word that softens the side (of the other) and removes hatred.

Muhdaran (brought forward): present on the Day of Resurrection.

Amadan ba'idan (a far-off term): a distant measure and far-reaching end.

Wa-yuhadhdhirukum Allahu nafsahu (and Allah warns you of Himself): i.e., He makes you fear His punishment if you disobey Him.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah, exalted is He, forbids His believing servants from taking the disbelievers as awliya', that is, helpers and supporters who exchange love and support against their believing brothers. He informed them, exalted is He, that whoever does this has been disowned by Allah, exalted is He, because of his disbelief and apostasy, since he has allied himself with the enemies of Allah and shown enmity to His allies. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. And whoever does that has nothing with Allah at all﴾, meaning Allah is free of him, his connection is severed, and the bond of loyalty between him and Allah is cut off, and woe to him, his ruin. Then Allah, exalted is He, granted a concession to the weak believers who live under the authority of the disbelievers, that they may show them sweetness of tongue without (any) in their hearts or deeds, and thereby guard themselves against their evil and harm, through a word of appeasement and courtesy. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Except when you fear from them a fear [taqiyyah]...﴾. Since the matter of disavowal and loyalty is of great gravity, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾, meaning regarding your taking His enemies as allies against His allies. He informed them that the final return is to Him and not to anyone else, so let the disobedient beware of standing before Allah. He said: ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾.

This is what the first verse [28] contains. As for the second verse [29], Allah, exalted is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to say to the people, believers and disbelievers alike: ﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it...﴾ of love or hatred, of contentment or anger, so do not utter it or show it in any state, or whether you show it by word, deed or condition, He knows it, and He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and He will call to account for it and recompense for it, and He is over all things competent. Let the intelligent person then be mindful of Allah and fear Him, and not venture into His disobediences, especially the allying of His enemies over His allies. As for the third verse [30]: ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done...﴾, in it Allah, exalted is He, reminds His servants of the Day of Resurrection so that they may refrain from evil and desist from injustice and corruption. He says: remember the Day when every soul will find what it did of good brought forward, present to be rewarded for, and what it did of evil and wrong, also present, and its sight will distress it, so it will wish with its whole heart that between it and that there were a distance that cannot be reached. Allah, exalted is He, concludes His reminder and guidance with His saying ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾, emphasizing the first warning, and He ends the verse with His saying: ﴿And Allah is Kind to the servants﴾. How excellent is what He ended with, for were it not for this, the hearts of all worlds would fly away in terror and fear, so the Possessor of kindness to His servants is not despaired of His mercy.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of taking disbelievers as allies in every case.

2- Allying with disbelievers against believers is apostasy, disbelief, and disavowal by Allah, exalted is He.

3- The permissibility of taqiyyah in a state of weakness of the believers and strength of the disbelievers.

4- The obligation to beware of the punishment of Allah, exalted is He, by obeying Him.

5- The gravity of the situation on the Day of Resurrection and the obligation to prepare for it through faith and piety.

Muhdaran (brought forward): present on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 31–32:

Explanation of the words:

"Tuhibbuna Allah" (you love Allah): for His perfect essence and His bounty upon you.

"Yuhbibkum Allah" (Allah will love you): for your obedience to Him and the purity of your souls through His fear.

"Yaghfir lakum dhunubakum" (He will forgive you your sins): He will cover them for you and not hold you accountable for them.

"Fa-in tawallaw" (but if they turn away): they turn away from faith and obedience.

The meaning of the two verses:

When the delegation of the Christians of Najran claimed that their glorifying of the Messiah and their sanctifying of him and his mother was only a way of seeking the love of Allah, by loving what He loves and glorifying what He glorifies, Allah commanded His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) in this verse to say to them: "If you truly love Allah, then follow me in what I have brought of monotheism and worship, and Allah will love you and also forgive you your sins, for He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful." Thereby He refuted their claim that they had not made the Messiah (peace be upon him) a god except in seeking the love of Allah and attaining it. And He guided them to the best path for attaining the love of Allah, which is to follow the Messenger in what he brought of faith, monotheism and worship that purifies the soul and brings about the love of Allah. This is what the first verse [31] contains. As for the second verse [32], Allah commanded His Messenger to tell the delegation of the Christians of Najran and others among the People of the Book and the polytheists to obey Him and obey His Messenger, for these two are the path to perfection and happiness in this world and the Hereafter. If they refuse and turn away, or turn their backs, then they have earned the wrath of Allah and His anger upon them, because they are disbelievers, and Allah does not love the disbelievers. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The love of the servant for the Lord, may He be exalted, is an obligation and a part of faith, based on the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Love Allah for the blessings He nourishes you with, and love me with the love of Allah," and his saying (ﷺ): "None of you truly believes until Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything else."

2- The love of Allah for the servant is the ultimate goal that people of knowledge strive for in life.

3- The way to obtain the love of Allah for the servant is to follow the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) by believing in what he brought, following his law, and obeying him in ease and in hardship, based on the verse ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me, and Allah will love you﴾. For it is not the matter that the servant should be loved, but rather the matter that he should love!

4- Claiming the love of Allah and His Messenger while opposing their command and prohibition is a false claim, and its bearer is certainly a loser.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 33–37:

Explanation of the words:

"Isṭafā Ādam" (chose Adam): chose; Ādam is the father of humankind, peace be upon him.

"Āl Ibrāhīm" (the family of Abraham): the āl of a man are his family and his followers upon his true religion.

ʿImrān: a righteous man among the righteous of the Children of Israel in their final era; he is the husband of Ḥannah and the father of Mary, peace be upon them both.

"Al-ʿĀlamīn" (the worlds): the people contemporary with them.

Imraʾat ʿImrān: Ḥannah.

"Nadhartu laka mā fī baṭnī" (I have vowed to You what is in my womb): she bound herself to dedicate it to Allah, to worship Him and serve His House, which is the Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House in Jerusalem).

"Muḥarraran" (dedicated): purely devoted, with no partnership in it for anyone other than Allah, such that it would never benefit from it.

Maryam: "servant of the Lord, exalted is He."

"Aʿīdhuhā bika" (I seek refuge for her in You): I protect her and guard her, under Your care, from Satan.

"Wa-kafalahā Zakariyyā" (and Zechariah took charge of her): Zechariah is the father of Yaḥyā, peace be upon them both, and his wife was a sister of Ḥannah.

"Al-miḥrāb" (the sanctuary): a chamber adjoining the mosque.

"Annā laki hādhā?" (From where is this for you?): from where did this come to you, i.e., from where did it come to you?

Meaning of the verses:

When the Christians of the delegation of Najrān claimed what they claimed about the Messiah, peace be upon him, namely his divinity and the divinity of his mother, Allah the Exalted revealed these verses, clarifying the origin of the matter of ʿĪsā and his mother and the reality of their situation. He, exalted is He, informed that He chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of ʿImrān, choosing them for His religion and selecting them for His worship, and thereby favoured them over the people. He informed that they are descendants of one another, their creeds not having differed and their virtues and spiritual perfections not having diverged, and that this is due to Allah's preservation of them and His care for them. He, exalted is He, informed that He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, meaning He hears the words of the wife of ʿImrān and knows her condition when she said: "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated..." That was because she was barren, and she saw in the garden of her house a bird feeding its young; she yearned for a child and asked her Lord to grant her a child and to let her dedicate it to worship Him and serve His House. Allah answered her, so she conceived; her husband died while she was pregnant, and she said what Allah related of her words: "When the wife of ʿImrān said: My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated, so accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." When the time of delivery came, she gave birth to a female and not a male, so she was grieved by this, and said: "My Lord, I have given birth to a female, and Allah knows best what she has given birth to." And how could He not know, when He is the Creator, the All-Knowing? She also said: "...and the male is not like the female..." in regard to service in the Holy House; therefore she was deeply regretful. She named her daughter Maryam, meaning servant of Allah, and asked her Lord to protect her and her offspring from the accursed Satan. Allah answered her, protected her and protected her son ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, so that no devil ever touched him. Allah accepted what she had vowed to Him, namely Mary, and caused her to grow in a good growth, and she grew up in a wondrous way, unlike ordinary infants. Zechariah took charge of her and she was raised in the house of her aunt. When Ḥannah had given birth to her, she nursed her, wrapped her in her swaddling clothes, and sent her to the righteous men of the Children of Israel so that they might entrust her to whoever they saw fit to raise her in his house, because her mother had dedicated her to Allah and it was not proper for her to keep her in her own house, and her father had also died. Each one wished to take charge of her, and Zechariah took charge of her, and she came to be in the house of her aunt by Allah's arrangement for her. When she grew up, he brought her into the sanctuary to worship there, and he would bring her food, and he would find with her summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer. He would be amazed by this and ask her, saying: "O Mary, from where is this for you?" She would answer him: "It is from Allah," and would account for it, saying: "Indeed Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning."

Lessons from the verses:

1- Clarification of Allah's bounty and favour upon whomever He wills.

2- Clarification that ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, is not the son of Allah, nor is he Allah, nor a third of three, but rather he is the servant of Allah and His messenger, whose mother is Mary; his grandmother is Ḥannah, and his grandfather is ʿImrān, from a house of nobility and righteousness among the Children of Israel.

3- Allah's answering the supplication of His friends, as He answered Ḥannah, granted her a child, and protected her daughter and her grandson from the accursed Satan.

4- The legitimacy of vowing to Allah, which is the believer's binding of himself to obedience in drawing near to Allah.

5- Clarification of the superiority of the male over the female in undertaking works and duties.

6- The permissibility of grief and regret over the good that a servant had hoped for and missed.

7- The establishment of the miracles (karāmāt) of the saints, as occurred for Mary in her sanctuary.

8- Affirmation of the prophethood of Muḥammad (ﷺ), since such accounts could not be related by an unlettered man except that he is a messenger to whom revelation is sent. This is why it was concluded with His words: "That is among the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you" [Āl ʿImrān: 44].

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (*Aysar al-Tafasir*) on Surah 3, verses 38–41:**

**Explanation of the words:**

**Hunalika (هنالك):** There, at that place, when he saw God's favor to Maryam (peace be upon her).

**Zakariyya (زكريا):** One of the prophets and messengers of the Children of Israel.

**Hab li (هب لي):** Give me.

**Min ladunka (من لدنك):** From You.

**Dhurriyya tayyiba (ذريّة طيبة):** Pure, righteous offspring.

**Bi-kalima min Allah (بكلمة من الله):** This is Jesus (peace be upon him), because he came into being by God's word "Be" (كُن).

**Wa sayyidan wa ḥaṣūran (وسيداً وحصوراً):** Noble, possessing knowledge and forbearance, with no desire for women due to the scarcity of his semen.

**Ghulam (غلام):** A male child.

**Aqir (عاقر):** Barren, unable to bear children due to sterility and infertility.

**Ayah (آية):** A sign by which he would know that conception had begun, so that he could give thanks for Your blessing.

**Illa ramzan (إلا رمزاً):** Except by gesture, a sign with the head or hand, understood in the same way as speech.

**Al-ibkar (الإبكار):** The beginning of the day; al-'ashiyy (العشي) is its end.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When Zakariyya witnessed God's marvels bestowed on Maryam, that she was given summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, he realized that God may give whatever He wills to whomever He wills, outside the ordinary order of natural laws. Thus his old age and his wife's barrenness did not prevent God from granting him a child. So he asked his Lord for a child, and his Lord answered him. While he was standing in prayer in his sanctuary (miḥrab), the angels gave him the good news, saying: "Indeed, God gives you good news of a son named Yahya, confirming a word from God," meaning that he would confirm Jesus son of Maryam and follow his path, because Jesus is "the Word," since God said to him "Be" and he was. He described him as a master, endowed with knowledge, forbearance, piety, and chastity, one who would not approach women, and a prophet among the righteous.

When Zakariyya heard the good news from the angels, Satan came to him and said: "What you heard as good news is from Satan. Had it come from the Most Merciful, He would have revealed it to you as a revelation." Here Zakariyya wished to verify the news, so he said: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren?﴾ So it was revealed to him that this is the doing of God, and God does what He wills. Then Zakariyya said: "My Lord, make for me a sign," meaning a sign by which he could know that conception had occurred, so that he might receive the blessing with gratitude. His Lord answered him, saying: ﴿Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days,﴾ meaning that you will wake up unable to speak for three days, so you will be unable to address anyone except by gesture, which will be understood from you. God then commanded him to meet this favor with complete gratitude, saying: ﴿And remember your Lord much, and glorify Him,﴾ meaning: pray in the evening, at the end of the day, and in the morning, at its beginning.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Learning from others' experiences: Zakariyya prayed for a child when he saw God's favor to Maryam.

2. The legitimacy of supplication, and that a private supplication is closer to being answered; and likewise when it is made during prayer.

3. Iblis may deceive a believer, but God removes his scheming and his whispering.

4. The permissibility of asking for a righteous child.

5. God's favors to His friends (awliya'), by answering their supplications.

6. The virtue of frequent remembrance of God, and the excellence of the two prayers of dawn and afternoon. In a hadith: "Whoever prays the two cool prayers will enter Paradise."

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 3, verses 42–44:**

**Explanation of the words:**

"And when the angels said": Tell the delegation of the Christians of Najran what the angels said, for that is evidence of the truth of your prophethood, of your truthfulness regarding the matter of Tawhid (the oneness of God), and of the fact that Jesus is not divine.

"Chose you" (istafaka): He selected you for His worship and for excellent obedience to Him.

"Purified you" (tahharaka): from sins and all other defects that would impair your closeness to God, Most High.

"Chosen you above the women of the worlds" (istafaka 'ala nisa' al-'alamin): That is, He preferred you over the women of the worlds through the honour He granted you, namely the birth of Jesus without a father.

"Be obedient" (iqnuti): Obey your Lord, be devoutly obedient to Him, and be humble.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 3, verses 45–47:

Explanation of the words:

Yubashshiruki (yubashshiruka): He informs you with news that is pleasing and joyful to you.

Bi-kalimatin minhu (by a word from Him): This is al-Masih, peace be upon him, and he was called a "word" because he came into being by the word of Allah the Exalted, ﴿Be!﴾ (kun).

Al-Masih (the Messiah): A title of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, and among its meanings is "the truthful" (al-siddiq).

Wajih (honoured): One who possesses rank, standing, and nobility among people.

Fi al-mahd (in the cradle): The mahd is the bed of the infant, who is still a suckling.

Wa-kahlan (and in maturity): Kuhula (maturity) is the age between youth and old age.

Wa-lam yamsisni basharun (and no man has touched me): She means that no male has approached her, neither for intercourse nor for anything else, and this is due to her being barren and her distance from unrelated men.

Qada amran (He decrees a matter): He willed it and decreed its existence.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the argument against the delegation of the Christians of Najran, when Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger: "And mention to them when the angels said: O Maryam, ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him﴾ ..." The verse. The angels, namely Jibril, peace be upon him, informed her that Allah the Exalted gives her good tidings of a child who will come into being by the word of Allah the Exalted, whose name is al-Masih ʿIsa son of Maryam, and that he will be honoured and noble in this world and in the Hereafter and among those brought near. He will speak to people while in the cradle at the time of nursing, just as he speaks to them in his youth and maturity, and he will be among the righteous who fulfil the rights of Allah the Exalted and the rights of His servants in full, without deficiency. Maryam replied, saying: ﴿My Lord, how can there be a child for me?﴾ That is, how can I have a child when no man has touched me in intercourse, and the way of Allah in creating a child is by such union? Jibril answered her, saying: The matter is thus; Allah the Exalted will create from you a child without a father. He, glory be to Him, creates what He wills, and when He decrees the existence of a thing that does not have causes, He says to it "Be," and it is, as Allah the Exalted has decreed and willed.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The clarification of Maryam's nobility and honour before her Lord, since Jibril spoke to her and gave her good tidings after appearing to her in the form of a man.

2- The clarification of the nobility and high standing of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, in this world and the Hereafter, and that he is among those brought near and the righteous.

3- ʿIsa speaking in the cradle is a sign from the signs of Allah the Exalted, since it is not the custom that an infant speaks during the time of nursing.

4- The permissibility of asking for clarification about what is contrary to custom, in order to know its secret, its cause, or its wisdom.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 48–51:

Explanation of the words:

al-Kitab: the writing and the script.

al-Hikmah (wisdom): correct knowledge, soundness in affairs, and understanding of the secrets of divine legislation.

Wa-rasulan: meaning, "and We will send him as a messenger."

Ayah (sign): a clear indication of his messengerhood and the truth of his prophethood.

Akhluqu lakum: meaning, "I will shape for you," not the creation which is origination and invention, since that belongs to Allah alone, exalted is He.

Ka-hay'at al-tayr: like the form of a bird.

Al-akmah: one born blind.

Al-abras: one afflicted with leprosy (baras), a chronic disease that ancient and modern medicine have been unable to cure; baras is a whiteness that afflicts human skin.

Tadakhirun: you withhold and conceal from your children food and other things.

Lima bayna yadayya: before me.

Inna Allaha rabbi wa-rabbukum: my God and your God, so worship Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to clarify the reality of Jesus, peace be upon him, that he is a servant of Allah and His messenger, and not the son of Allah nor a god alongside Allah. Allah, exalted is He, informs that He creates him by the word "Be," and teaches him the Book, the wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel, and this has happened. He sends him as a messenger to the Children of Israel, and this has happened. Jesus informed them that he had come to them with a sign from their Lord indicating the truth of his messengerhood: he shapes for them from clay the form of a bird, then breathes into it, and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission. He heals the one born blind and the leper, and raises the dead by Allah's permission, and indeed he would wipe over one with a persistent affliction such as leprosy, and its owner would be healed immediately. They asked him to bring back to life for them Sam ibn Nuh, and he brought him to life by Allah's permission. He informs them of what they eat in their houses and what they store, and he never errs. Then he said to them: indeed, in that which has been mentioned there is a sign for you indicating my truth, if you are believers, so believe in me and do not deny me. I have come to you confirming what is before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you, and in that is good for you and mercy, so believe in me. They denied him, so he said to them: fear Allah and obey me, and you will be saved and made happy. Finally, he informed them that Allah, exalted is He, is his Lord and their Lord, and that they must worship Him in order to be perfected and made happy, and that the worship of Allah alone and in accordance with what He has legislated is the straight path that leads those who travel it to perfection and happiness in both lives.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The nobility and virtue of writing.

2- The excellence of wisdom, which is deep understanding of the secrets of the Law and soundness in affairs.

3- The unseen belongs to Allah, and He teaches His prophets of it what He wills.

4- The affirmation of the miracles of Jesus, peace be upon him.

5- There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and Jesus is the word of Allah and a spirit from Him and a messenger to the Children of Israel.

6- The command to piety and obedience to the Messenger, since happiness and perfection depend upon them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 52–58:

Explanation of the words:

Ahassa minhumu al-kufr (ﷺ perceived disbelief in them): he knew of their disbelief and of what he had brought, and of their intent to harm him.

Al-hawariyyun (the disciples; sing. hawari): plural of hawari, and what is meant by them is his chosen ones and his companions.

Muslimun (submitting): submitting to the command of God and His Messenger, obedient.

Al-shahidin (the witnesses): those who testify that there is no god but God, and who worship Him in the manner in which He must be worshipped.

Makaru (they plotted): they plotted the killing of the Messiah, peace be upon him.

Wa-makara Allah (and God planned): God, exalted is He, planned for his deliverance and frustrated them in what they had resolved upon.

Khayr al-makirin (the best of planners): the best of those who plan for the rescue of His allies and the destruction of His enemies.

Mutawaffika (I will complete for you): completing for you what I have decreed for you of the days of your remaining with your people.

Wa-rafi'uka ilayya (and raising you to Me): to My presence in the highest dominion.

Wa-mutahhiruka (and purifying you): keeping you far removed from their filth and disbelief.

Dhalika natluhu 'alayk (That which We recite to you): that aforementioned account of Jesus, which We recite to you from among the verses of the Wise Qur'an.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in debate with the delegation of the Christians of Najran. He, exalted is He, mentioned that when Jesus knew of his people's disbelief and their intent to kill him secretly, he called upon the believers, saying: ﴿Who are my helpers for God?﴾ So the disciples, who were his chosen and beloved ones, answered him, saying: ﴿We are God's helpers. We believe in God, and bear witness, O Spirit of God, that we are submitting.﴾ ﴿Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and we follow the Messenger, so write us among the witnesses﴾ to Your oneness and to the messengership of Your messengers. He, exalted is He, said: The Jews carried out their plot by besieging the dwelling of Jesus in order to seize him and crucify him. God, exalted is He, planned, and He is the best of planners, when He said to His servant and messenger Jesus: "I will cause you to die," that is, I will take you and raise you to My presence. Then God took him, brought him out through the window of the house, raised him to Himself, and cast the likeness upon the chief of the attacking guard, so they thought he was the Messiah and killed him and crucified him. Glory be to the Planner, the Wise. And so: ﴿And they plotted, and God plotted, and God is the best of plotters.﴾ His saying to him, "and purifying you from those who disbelieve," means: clearing him of the false accusations of the Jews when they said he was a sorcerer and the son of adultery, and keeping him far from the sphere of their community, which had rotted with disbelief, wickedness, corruption. He promised him that He would make those who followed him in what he brought of faith, Islam and excellence superior to those who disbelieved in that until the Day of Resurrection. God, exalted is He, has fulfilled His promise: He honored the people of Islam and gave them victory, and humbled and disgraced the Jews and disbelievers. He also promised him that He would return all of them to Himself on the Day of Resurrection and judge between them concerning what they differed over in the world, of faith and disbelief, righteousness and corruption, and repay each group for what they earned of good or evil. So He said: ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ. As for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment﴾ in this world by killing, captivity, humiliation and destitution, and in the Hereafter with the punishment of the Fire, and they will have no helpers to rescue them from Our punishment. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them in full the rewards of their faith and righteous deeds: in this world, victory and establishment, and in the Hereafter, gardens and bliss. God, mighty and majestic, does not love the wrongdoers; how then would He wrong His servants when He recompenses them for their deeds? He does not wrong any of His servants, believer or disbeliever, even by the weight of an atom, but He repays by His justice and shows mercy by His grace.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The establishment of the proof against the Christians of Najran, since the Messenger ﷺ informed them by revelation, and thereby affirmed the falsehood of the divinity of Jesus, peace be upon him, by mentioning his attributes and his circumstances with his people, and God's honoring him and those who followed him, both in this world and the next.

2- Islam is the religion of the prophets and of all human nations, and there is no other true religion; every religion other than it is false.

3- Confirmation of the Messenger ﷺ's report that every prophet has disciples and helpers.

4- The virtue of the people of "There is no god but God," since they are the witnesses to the truth and those who speak it.

5- Affirmation that God took Jesus and raised him to Himself alive, and that he will descend at the end of the world to rule for a time, then die the death that God has decreed for every human being; God did not combine two deaths for him. This is evidence that he was raised to heaven alive, not dead.

6- The truthfulness of God's promise of honor to the people of Islam and the humiliation of the Jews throughout life.
