Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 59–63:

Explanation of the words:

Al-mathal (المثل): the strange and wondrous attribute.

Al-haqq min rabbika (الحق من ربك): that which We have related to you concerning ʿĪsā (Jesus) is the established truth from your Lord.

Al-mumtarin (الممترين): the doubters, since imtira' (الامتراء) means doubt.

Hajjaka (حاجك): argued with you using proofs.

Nabtahil (نبتهل): we invoke a curse, i.e., we curse whichever of us is lying.

Al-qasas al-haqq (القصص الحق): what God Most High has related is the true narrative, established and free of doubt.

Al-mufsidun (المفسدون): those who commit acts of disobedience to God Most High on earth, such as polytheism and major sins.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish the servanthood of ʿĪsā and his messengership, not his lordship or divinity. It is reported that the delegation of Najran said to the Messenger ﷺ, among what they said: "Every human has a father, so what is the matter with ʿĪsā, who has no father?" So God Most High revealed to His Messenger: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of ʿĪsā before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ So he is existent. Then what is the call to take ʿĪsā as a god? Because he was created by God without a father, Adam was likewise created without a father or a mother, and he came to be only by the word of God. Similarly, ʿĪsā was created by the word of God, which is "Be," and he was. This is the established truth from God Most High concerning ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, so do not be among the doubters about it; and far be it from him ﷺ to doubt.

When they persisted greatly in disputing and arguing with him ﷺ, his Lord Most High guided him to a way of ending their dispute, which is mubahalah (mutual imprecation): that they gather together and each party says, "O God, curse whichever of us is lying." Whoever is lying among them will perish immediately. So his Lord Most High said to him: ﴿Whoever argues with you concerning him after the knowledge has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke earnestly and place the curse of God upon the liars."﴾ On the next day the Messenger of God ﷺ went out with al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah, may God be pleased with them all. However, the Christians recognized the truth and feared that if they cursed, they would perish, so they fled from the mubahalah. The Messenger ﷺ invited them to Islam, but they refused and were content with disbelief, out of preserving their leadership and their worldly interests, and they agreed to a settlement, committing themselves to paying the jizyah to the Muslims and remaining upon their false religion.

Then God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ — referring to what We have related to you concerning ʿĪsā, peace be upon him: that he is the servant of God and His messenger, His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him; and that there is no god but God, i.e., there is no worshipped one in truth except Him, Most High. Indeed God is the Mighty, the Victorious, whom nothing can prevent from what He wills, the Wise in His creation and His management. Then He threatened the Christians of Najran and others among the people of corruption on earth, that He knows them well and will soon bring His vengeance upon them and send down His curse upon them, and He is powerful over everything.

Guidance from the verses:

1- God's care for His Messenger, by guiding him to the method by which he ended the Christians' disputation, which had pained and wearied him.

2- The legitimacy of mubahalah, though it is to be undertaken by the righteous whose supplications are answered.

3- Affirmation of God's divinity alone, and the falsehood of the Christians' claim of deifying ʿĪsā, peace be upon him.

4- God's warning to the people of corruption on earth, namely those who engage in polytheism and sins.

Al-mumtarin (الممترين): the doubters, since imtira' (الامتراء) means doubt.

Hajjaka (حاجك): argued with you using proofs.

Nabtahil (نبتهل): we invoke a curse, i.e., we curse whichever of us is lying.

Al-qasas al-haqq (القصص الحق): what God Most High has related is the true narrative, established and free of doubt.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 64–68:

Explanation of the words:

Ahl al-Kitab (People of the Book): the Jews and the Christians, because the Jews possess the Torah and the Christians possess the Gospel (Injil).

Ila kalimatin sawa' (to a common word): al-kalima al-sawa' is the just word, namely that we worship God alone, without partner, and that some of us do not take others as lords (arbab) besides God.

Arbaban (lords): arbab is the plural of rabb, meaning one who is worshipped and obeyed without obedience to God, the Exalted.

Fa-in tawallaw (but if they turn away): they turn away from monotheism (tawhid).

Ishhadu (bear witness): know, with the knowledge of sight and direct observation, that we are Muslims.

Tuhajjuna (you argue): you dispute with false proofs.

Yahudiyyan wa-la nasraniyyan (a Jew or a Christian): Abraham was not upon the religion of the Jews, nor upon the religion of the Christians.

Kana hanifan musliman (he was a hanif, a Muslim): inclining away from false creeds toward the religion of truth, which is Islam.

Awla al-nas bi-Ibrahim (closest of people to Abraham): most entitled in relation to Abraham and his allegiance, namely those who followed him in monotheism.

Wa-Allahu wali al-mu'minin (God is the Protector of the believers): the one who manages their affairs and gives them victory.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to refute the falsehood of the two groups of People of the Book. God said to His Messenger: Say to them, O People of the Book, Jews and Christians, "Come" — rise up from the pit of falsehood in which you are fallen — "to a common word," a just word, on which we agree: that we worship God alone and associate nothing with Him, and that some of us do not take others as lords besides God, imposing obedience on one another and requiring prostration in reverence and sanctification. If they refuse this and turn away, then say, O believers: "Bear witness, O you who turn away from the truth, that we are Muslims." This contains an allusion, rather an explicit statement, that others are not Muslims.

This is the meaning of the first verse [64]. As for the second verse [65], God commands His Messenger likewise to say to those who turn away from the truth: O People of the Book, why do you argue about Abraham, when each group among you claims that Abraham was upon its religion, although Judaism was not except after the revelation of the Torah, and Christianity was not except after the revelation of the Gospel, while Abraham came hundreds of years before the two Books were revealed? Why do you say what is neither accepted nor reasonable? "Will you not then use your reason?" Then He rebuked them with what they deserve, saying to them: Listen, O people, you have argued about what you have knowledge of concerning your religion and your Book, yet you argue about what you have no knowledge of concerning Abraham and his upright religion, which was founded on the principle of monotheism and sincere worship of God alone. God knows of Abraham and his religion what you do not know, and it is not your right to speak about what you do not know. Then He refuted them after rebuking them, saying: "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif, a monotheist, obedient to his Lord, a Muslim submitting to Him, and he was not among the polytheists." After God had rebuked those who argued with His Messenger and denied their claim that Abraham was upon their religion, He established a great truth which they ought to know and acknowledge: that the people most entitled to Abraham and to belonging to him are those who followed him in the creed of monotheism and the worship of God, the Exalted, according to what He prescribed. These are this noble and great Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and those who believed with him and followed the guidance he brought. God, the Exalted, is the Protector of the believers and the Enemy of the disbelievers and polytheists.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The condition of humanity will not be set right, nor its affairs upright, except when it adopts the principle of the common word, which is that it worship its Lord alone and associate nothing with Him, and that some of it not exalt itself over others under any law or slogan.

2- The authority of history and the demonstration of the need for it: God answered the People of the Book in their claim that Abraham was upon their religion by pointing out that the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after his death, so how could he be a Jew or a Christian?

3- The condemnation of one who argues about what he has no knowledge of and no concern with.

4- Judaism, like Christianity, was not the religion of God, the Exalted; rather, they are two innovations and nothing more.

5- Believers are allies of one another, even if their homelands are distant and their regions far apart, and God is the Protector of the believers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 69–71:

Explanation of the words:

"Wadat ta'ifatun" (A group wished): a party wished, namely the rabbis and the leaders among them.

"Law yudilluunakum" (If only they could lead you astray): that is, they wished to cause you to fall into misguidance so that you would be wretched and perish like them.

"Wa ma yash'uruun" (And they do not perceive): that is, they do not realize or know that by attempting to mislead the believers, they are only misguiding themselves, since they plunge deeper into evil, and so their punishment is multiplied.

"Labs al-haqq bil-batil" (Mixing truth with falsehood): mixing it with it, as if clothing falsehood in the garment of truth and clothing truth in the garment of falsehood, so that it is not recognized and acted upon, nor is guidance sought through it.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah, exalted is He, informs His believing servants that a group of the People of the Book wished that they could lead you into misguidance so that you would perish. Most likely this group consists of their leaders, rabbis and priests, although most Jews and Christians wish to mislead the Muslims out of envy for the truth they hold. Allah informs us that by wishing the destruction of the Muslims, they are in fact destroying themselves, and they do not perceive this or know it. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 72–74:

Explanation of the words:

Wajh al-nahar wa akhirahu (the beginning and end of the day): its beginning, which is the morning, and its end, which is the evening.

Wa la tu'minu illa li-man tabi'a dinakum (and do not believe except one who follows your religion): i.e., do not give credence except to one who is upon your creed (millah).

Al-huda huda Allah (guidance is the guidance of God): the true clarification and complete success are the clarification and guidance of God, not what the Jews mix in and dress up as deception to mislead people.

An yu'ta ahadun mithla ma utitum (that anyone be given the like of what you have been given): that anyone be given prophethood, religion and excellence.

Aw yuhajjukum 'inda rabbikum (or they argue with you before your Lord): they dispute with you on the Day of Resurrection before your Lord.

Qul inna al-fadla biyadi Allah (say: excellence is in the hand of God): say: success in faith and guidance to Islam are in the hand of God, not in the hand of anyone else.

Wa Allahu wasi'un 'alim (and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing): possessor of abundance through His bounty, knowing who deserves His bounty, so He bestows it upon him.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, informs of the scheming and deception of the Jews against the Muslims, saying: ﴿And a group of the People of the Book said: "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end; perhaps they will turn back."﴾ This is because Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Malik ibn al-Sayf, may the curse of God be upon them, said to some of their brethren: "Pray with the Muslims the dawn prayer facing the Ka'bah, and pray the afternoon prayer facing the Rock of Jerusalem. If you are asked, 'Why did you turn away from the Ka'bah after you had prayed toward it?' say to them: 'It has become clear to us that the truth is facing the Rock, not the Ka'bah.'" This is the meaning of His saying concerning them: ﴿And a group of the People of the Book said: "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe"﴾, meaning regarding the matter of the qiblah. ﴿At the beginning of the day﴾, i.e., in the morning. ﴿And disbelieve at its end﴾, i.e., deny it in the evening. ﴿Perhaps they will turn back﴾, i.e., to facing the Rock instead of the Ka'bah. The aim was to confuse the thinking of the Muslims and to introduce doubt among them.

His saying concerning them: ﴿And do not believe except one who follows your religion﴾ means that they said to one another: do not give credence to anyone except one who follows your religion, from among the people of your creed. This is a diversion by their leaders from Islam and from accepting it, i.e., do not believe the Muslims in what they tell you. Here God responds to them, saying: "Say, O Our Messenger: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God," not the error that the Jews monopolize, claiming it to be the truth and guidance, which is the Jewish innovation.

His saying: ﴿that anyone be given the like of what you have been given, or they argue with you before your Lord﴾ is the speech of the Jews, coordinated with their saying: ﴿And do not believe except one who follows your religion.﴾ As for His saying ﴿Say: "Indeed, the guidance…"﴾, it is an interjected statement between the words of the Jews, placed earlier for the sake of a hasty response to them. The meaning of their saying ﴿that anyone be given…﴾ etc. is: they dislike that anyone from among you should acknowledge that Muhammad is a true prophet and that his religion is true, so that the Jews and the polytheists would follow him and submit; or at least that the Muslims would remain firm upon it. We wish to shake them and cause them doubt until they return to the religion of their fathers. Or "they argue with you before your Lord" on the Day of Resurrection, and they will have the proof against you if you acknowledge to them today that their prophet is true and their religion is true. Therefore they persist in insisting that there is no true religion except Judaism and that anything other than it is false.

Here God commands His Messenger to say to them, rebuking them: ﴿Indeed, excellence is in the hand of God﴾, not in the hand of the Jews, ﴿He gives it﴾, i.e., the excellence which is prophethood, guidance and success, and what follows from that of the good of this world and the Hereafter, ﴿to whom He wills﴾ of His servants, and withholds it from whom He wills. He is the One of wide bounty, the All-Knowing of whom is worthy and deserving of it. ﴿He singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾

Guidance from the verses:

1- Recording the scheming and deception of the Jews, which is a characteristic of theirs that remains with them until the Day of Resurrection.

2- Unveiling Jewish fanaticism and methods of obfuscation and misleading, and global media today is a manifestation of Jewish misleading.

3- The extreme naivety of the Jews in understanding matters of religion and belief, which they have inherited down to today; for what believer in God and the Last Day would say: "Do not acknowledge to the Muslims that they are upon the truth, lest they argue against you with your acknowledgment on the Day of Resurrection"?

God, the Exalted, knows that the Jews deny Islam, which is the truth, and disbelieve in it, though it is the truth from their Lord, and that He will punish them in the Fire of Hell, where they will abide forever. So, does their not openly telling the Muslims that they are upon the truth, while they know that they are upon the truth in their religion, save them from God's punishment for their disbelief in Islam? No indeed. What, then, is the meaning of their saying: "Do not acknowledge Islam, lest the Muslims argue against you with your acknowledgment on the Day of Resurrection"?? It is ignorance and naivety in understanding. Glory be to God, what wonders there are in creation!!

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 75–77:

Explanation of the words:

*In ta'manhu* (إن تأمنه): *i'tamanahu 'ala kadhā* means he placed it with him as a trust (amanah) and entrusted him with it, so he did not fear him concerning it.

*Qinṭār* (قنطار): a known measure of weight; what is meant here is that it is of gold, as shown by the mention of the dinar.

*Illā mā dumta 'alayhi qā'iman* (إلا ما دمت عليه قائماً): i.e., persistently, pursuing him for it night and day.

*Al-ummiyyīn* (الأمّيين): the idolatrous Arabs.

*Sabīl* (سبيل): i.e., Allah will not hold us to account if we consume their wealth, because they are polytheists.

*Balā* (بلى): i.e., the matter is not as the Jews claim, that there is no blame or sin upon them for consuming the wealth of the idolatrous Arabs; rather, they bear sin and accountability.

*Lā khalāq lahum* (لا خلاق لهم): i.e., they have no share or portion in the good things of the Hereafter and the bliss of the Gardens.

*Lā yuzakkīhim* (لا يزكيهم): He does not purify them from their sins nor expiate them for them.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in exposing the People of the Book and explaining their diseased souls and blameworthy qualities. In this verse [75], Allah, exalted is He, informs that among the Jews are those who, if you entrust them with a great amount of wealth, will return it to you in full, and among them are those who, if you entrust them with a dinar or less, will betray you concerning it and deny it to you, so they will not return it to you except when you pursue them for it and persistently press them. Allah, exalted is He, addressing His Messenger, said: ﴿Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you unless you persistently stand over him﴾. The Lord, exalted is He, explains this conduct of theirs by their saying ﴿There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered ones﴾, i.e., there is no sin or blame upon us in consuming the wealth of the Arabs, because they are polytheists, so we are not held to account for consuming their wealth. Allah refuted this false claim, saying: ﴿And they speak falsehood against Allah while they know﴾, i.e., they lie against Allah, but they lie in order to justify their deceit and betrayal.

In the second verse [76], He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Yes [indeed]﴾, i.e., the matter is not as they claim; rather, they bear sin, blame and accountability. Whoever fulfills the covenant of Allah, exalted is He, by believing in His Messenger and what he brought, and guards against polytheism and sins, bears no sin, blame or accountability; this is the one whom Allah loves, so He does not punish him, for He, mighty and majestic, loves the God-fearing. As for the last verse [77], the Lord, exalted is He, threatens with the severest kinds of punishment those who make covenants and then betray them, swear oaths and lie for the sake of the worldly goods and its meager provision, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price—those will have no share in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., they have no portion or share in the bliss of the Last Abode, and He will not speak to them, as a mark of honor and dignity; nor will He purify them by praising them or cleansing them of their sins. For them is a painful punishment in the abode of wretchedness, a punishment that is lasting and enduring.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- One must not be deceived by the Jews, nor trust them, because of their known treachery.

2- Whoever lies against Allah is more deserving of lying to people.

3- A clarification of the Jewish belief that humanity other than Jews is impure, and that their wealth and honor are permissible and lawful for the Jews, since in their view they are the believers and others are disbelievers.

4- The gravity of the sin of one who breaks his covenant for the sake of wealth, and likewise one who swears falsely for the sake of wealth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever swears an oath by which he takes someone's property while he is lying in it, will meet Allah while He is angry with him."

*Lā khalāq lahum* (لا خلاق لهم): i.e., they have no share or portion in the good things of the Hereafter and the bliss of the Gardens.

*Lā yuzakkīhim* (لا يزكيهم): He does not purify them from their sins nor expiate them for them.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in exposing the People of the Book and explaining their diseased souls and blameworthy qualities. In this verse [75], Allah, exalted is He, informs that among the Jews are those who, if you entrust them with a great amount of wealth, will return it to you in full, and among them are those who, if you entrust them with a dinar or less, will betray you concerning it and deny it to you, so they will not return it to you except when you pursue them for it and persistently press them. Allah, exalted is He, addressing His Messenger, said: ﴿Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you unless you persistently stand over him﴾. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verse 78:

Explanation of the words:

"And indeed among them is a group": a faction of the Jews who were contemporaries of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the city of Medina.

"Distorting their tongues": they twist their tongues in speech, as if they were reading the Book (kitab).

"And it is not from the Book": and it is not from the Book.

"And they speak falsehood about Allah": that is, they lie about Allah for material ends.

The meaning of the verse:

The context remains concerning the Jews and the exposure of their disgraceful conduct. Allah the Exalted informs that a faction of them "distort their tongues" (yalwuna alsinatahum), meaning they twist their pronunciation of speech to deceive the listeners, as if they were reciting the Torah and what Allah revealed in it, while it is not from the revealed Book at all; rather, it is pure falsehood. They say to you, "It is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. They "speak falsehood about Allah" in order to preserve worthless worldly gain and false leadership.

Guidance from the verse

Among the guidance of this verse:

1- The exposure of the Jews' cunning, their misleading of people, and their deceiving them in the name of religion and knowledge.

2- The audacity of the Jews in lying to people and to Allah, while knowing that they are lying; and this is an extremely grave ugliness and a greater injustice.

3- A warning to the Muslim against the Jews' conduct of deception and of speaking about Allah and His Messenger for corrupt worldly aims.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 79–80:

Explanation of the words:

Ma kana li-bashar (It is not for a human being): It is not the case for a human being whom Allah gives the Book, the wisdom (hukm), and prophethood.

Al-kitab wa al-hukm wa al-nubuwwah (the Book, the wisdom, and prophethood): The Book is the written revelation of Allah. Al-hukm means hikmah (wisdom), which is understanding (fiqh) of the secrets of the Sharia. Al-nubuwwah is that with which Allah the Exalted honours His servant, by informing him of the unseen and speaking to him through revelation.

Rabbaniyyin (those devoted to the Lord): the plural of rabbani, one who is ascribed to the Lord (rabb) because of his abundant worship and profound knowledge, or ascribed to al-rabban, the one who trains people and sets their affairs right and attends to them.

Arbaban (lords): the plural of rabb, meaning master or object of worship.

Ya'murukum bi-al-kufr (would he order you to disbelief?): The interrogative is for denial, and kufr here means apostasy from Islam.

The meaning of the two verses:

The context continues in refutation of the People of the Book, and in this verse [79] there is a specific refutation of the delegation of the Christians of Najran, who deify the Messiah (peace be upon him). Allah the Exalted says: It is not the case for any human being whom Allah gives the Book, meaning He sends down a Book to him and grants him wisdom in it, which is understanding and comprehension of its secrets, and honours him with prophethood so that He reveals to him, and places him among His prophets, that he would then call people to worship himself, saying to people: "Be servants to me besides Allah." This never was and never will be. Nor is it even conceivable. So what is wrong with you, O Christians, that you believe this about the Messiah (peace be upon him)? Whoever is granted such perfection does not say to people, "Be servants to me," but rather says to them, "Be people devoted to the Lord, who reform people and guide them to their Lord, so that they may be perfected through obedience to Him and be happy by it," and that is by teaching them the Book, instructing in it, and studying it.

This is the meaning of verse [79]. As for verse [80], Allah the Exalted informs about His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) that he does not command people to worship anyone other than his Lord, the Exalted, whether that other be an honoured angel or a sent prophet. He denounces those who attributed this to him (ﷺ), saying: "Would he order you to disbelief after you have submitted [to Allah]?" Such a thing is not valid from him and does not proceed from him in any way.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- It is not possible for one whom Allah has given the Book and wisdom and honoured with prophethood to call people to worship himself, let alone to worship others.

2- The leaders of people are the rabbaniyyin, who train people through knowledge and wisdom, so that they set them right and guide them.

3- The great among people are those who teach people good and guide them to it.

4- Prostrating to other than Allah the Exalted is kufr, because it is reported that the verse was revealed in refutation of those who wanted to prostrate to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whereupon Allah the Exalted said: "Would he order you to disbelief after you have submitted [to Allah]?!"

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 3, verses 81–83:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*al-Mithaq* (the covenant): a pledge confirmed by oath.

*Lamma ataytukum* (whatever I have given you): *mahma ataytukum* (whatever I give you).

*Latu'minunna* (you shall surely believe in him): *latusaddiqunna* (you shall surely affirm his message).

*A-aqrartum* (did you acknowledge): the first hamzah is an interrogative of confirmation (*istifham taqriri*), and *aqrartum* means *i'taraftum* (you acknowledged).

*Isri* (my covenant): *ahdi wa mithaqi* (my pact and my covenant).

*Faman tawalla* (whoever turns away): *raja'a 'amma i'taraf bihi wa aqarra* (goes back on what he acknowledged and affirmed).

*Al-fasiqun* (the defiantly disobedient): *al-kharijun 'an ta'at Allah wa rasulihi* (those who leave the obedience of Allah and His Messenger).

*Afaghayra deen Allah yabghun* (is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek?): the interrogative is one of denunciation (*istifham lil-inkar*), and *yabghun* means *yatlubun* (they seek).

*Wa lahu aslam* (and to Him has submitted): *inqada wa khada'a limajari aqdar Allah wa ahkamihi 'alayh* (yielded and submitted to the courses of Allah's decrees and His rulings over him).

**Meaning of the verses:**

The context continues in the refutation of the Christians of Najran. Allah, the Exalted, says to His Messenger: mention to them the covenant that Allah took from the prophets and their peoples: that whatever book and wisdom He gives them, and then there comes to them a messenger confirming what is with them of light and guidance, they shall surely believe in him and surely support him against his enemies and opponents from among the people of disbelief. Allah, the Exalted, put them to the test, and they acknowledged and affirmed. Then He called them to witness concerning this, and they bore witness, and He Himself bore witness, saying: ﴿And I am with you among the witnesses﴾. Then Allah, the Exalted, emphasized this once more: whoever turns away from this covenant after it and does not fulfill it is considered defiantly disobedient and will receive the recompense of the defiantly disobedient. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then whoever turns away after that — those are the defiantly disobedient﴾.

Both the Jews and the Christians have broken this covenant, for they did not believe in Muhammad ﷺ or in what he brought, although the covenant to believe in him and to support him had been taken from them. They disbelieved in him and forsook him, and so by this they became the defiantly disobedient, deserving the punishment of Allah.

Then Allah, the Exalted, rebuked the People of the Book, saying: ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah﴾ — meaning Islam — ﴿that they seek?﴾ i.e., that they desire. And to Allah has submitted whoever is in the heavens, the angels, and whoever is on the earth, all the earthly creatures, whether willingly or unwillingly: obedient or compelled. And beyond this, to Him you will be returned, and He will call you to account and recompense you for your deeds.

This is what the last verse [83] contains, when Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?﴾

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Explanation of Allah's way with the earlier prophets: that some of them believe in others and support one another.

2. The disbelief and defiant disobedience of the People of the Book, through their breaking of the covenant and their turning away from Islam and their aversion to it after disbelieving in the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, though the covenant had been taken from them to believe in him and follow him.

3. Clarification of the great status of covenants and pledges with Allah, the Exalted.

4. Denunciation of those who turn away from the religion of Allah, Islam, although the whole universe is subject and submissive to the command of Allah and the courses of His decrees, submitting to Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 84–85:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Asbat (the tribes): plural of sibt (grandson). Here, al-asbat refers to the twelve sons of Ya'qub (Jacob), and the asbat among the Jews are like the tribes (qaba'il) among the Arabs.

Yabtaghi: seeks and desires a religion other than the religion of Islam.

Al-khasirin (the losers): those who are destroyed by abiding forever in the Fire of Hell, and those who have lost everything, even themselves.

The meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the argumentation with the People of the Book. After God rebuked them in the previous verses by saying: ﴿Do you seek other than the religion of God?﴾ (O company of Jews and Christians), if they say "Yes," then you, O our Messenger, say: "We believe in God and in what has been revealed to us of revelation and law, and we believe in what was revealed to Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, and what was revealed to his two sons Isma'il and Ishaq, and what was revealed to Ya'qub and his children, the tribes; and we believe in what was given to Musa of the Torah and to 'Isa of the Gospel, and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We do not make any distinction between any of His prophets, but we believe in them and in what they brought, and we do not believe in some and disbelieve in others, as is your condition, O company of Jews and Christians. And we are Muslims to God," meaning submissive and obedient, not worshipping Him except in the manner He has legislated, and not worshipping anything besides Him. This is the meaning of the first verse [84].

As for the second verse [85], God affirms that every religion other than Islam is invalid, and that whoever seeks a religion other than Islam will never have it accepted from him in any way, and in the Hereafter he will be among the great losers. So God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾, those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. That is the manifest loss.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The faith of a servant who believes in some of the messengers and disbelieves in others is not valid, just as the faith of a servant who believes in some of what God, the Exalted, revealed to His messengers and disbelieves in some of it is not valid.

2- Islam: it is submission and surrender to God, the Exalted, and it is incompatible with choosing among the messengers of God and His revelation to them.

3- The invalidity of all other religions and creeds apart from the religion of Islam and the community (millah) of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 84–85:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Asbat (the tribes): plural of sibt (grandson). Here, al-asbat refers to the twelve sons of Ya'qub (Jacob), and the asbat among the Jews are like the tribes (qaba'il) among the Arabs.

Yabtaghi: seeks and desires a religion other than the religion of Islam.

Al-khasirin (the losers): those who are destroyed by abiding forever in the Fire of Hell, and those who have lost everything, even themselves.

The meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the argumentation with the People of the Book. After God rebuked them in the previous verses by saying: ﴿Do you seek other than the religion of God?﴾ (O company of Jews and Christians), if they say "Yes," then you, O our Messenger, say: "We believe in God and in what has been revealed to us of revelation and law, and we believe in what was revealed to Abraham, the Friend of the Most Merciful, and what was revealed to his two sons Isma'il and Ishaq, and what was revealed to Ya'qub and his children, the tribes; and we believe in what was given to Musa of the Torah and to 'Isa of the Gospel, and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We do not make any distinction between any of His prophets, but we believe in them and in what they brought, and we do not believe in some and disbelieve in others, as is your condition, O company of Jews and Christians. And we are Muslims to God," meaning submissive and obedient, not worshipping Him except in the manner He has legislated, and not worshipping anything besides Him. This is the meaning of the first verse [84].

As for the second verse [85], God affirms that every religion other than Islam is invalid, and that whoever seeks a religion other than Islam will never have it accepted from him in any way, and in the Hereafter he will be among the great losers. So God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾, those who lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. That is the manifest loss.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The faith of a servant who believes in some of the messengers and disbelieves in others is not valid, just as the faith of a servant who believes in some of what God, the Exalted, revealed to His messengers and disbelieves in some of it is not valid.

2- Islam: it is submission and surrender to God, the Exalted, and it is incompatible with choosing among the messengers of God and His revelation to them.

3- The invalidity of all other religions and creeds apart from the religion of Islam and the community (millah) of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 86–89:

Explanation of the words:

﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief﴾: The interrogative here is for denying likelihood (istib'ad), and guidance (hidayah) is coming out of misguidance.

Al-bayyinat (the clear proofs): the proofs, including the miracles of the messengers and the verses of the Qur'an that make the truth clear in belief and in action.

Al-zalimin (the wrongdoers): those who exceed the limit in wrongdoing and go to extremes in it, until wrongdoing has become a fixed attribute of theirs.

La'nat Allah (the curse of Allah): Allah's expulsion of them from every good, and the curse of the angels and people is their supplication against them with that.

Wa la hum yunzarun (nor will they be reprieved): nor will they be given respite, for one who is given respite is granted delay and is not hastened in punishment.

Aslihu (make amends): they should set right what they have corrupted in themselves and in others.

The meaning of the verses:

The context remains concerning the People of the Book, although it also touches on others who apostatized from Islam, such as some of the Ansar who later returned to Islam, embraced it again, and whose Islam became sound. Concerning all of these, the Exalted says: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief﴾. The Jews disbelieved in Jesus, peace be upon him, although they bore witness that the Messenger Muhammad is true, and proofs and evidences of the truth of his prophethood and the soundness of the true religion he brought came to them. Allah, according to His sunnah in His creation, does not guide one who has greatly exceeded in wrongdoing and gone beyond the limit in it, so that wrongdoing has become a nature of his. Therefore, the guidance of one in this condition is considered extremely unlikely, though not impossible. Then the Exalted informed about them, threatening them, saying: ﴿Those—their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels and of mankind, all together﴾ ﴿abiding therein﴾, meaning in that curse which necessitates for them the punishment of the Fire. ﴿The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved﴾, meaning they will not be given time to make excuses, or the punishment will not be lightened for them. Then, since their repentance is not impossible, and because Allah the Exalted loves the repentance of His servants and accepts it from them, the Exalted said, opening the door of His mercy to His servants whatever their sins: ﴿Except those who repent after that﴾ (the disbelief and wrongdoing), ﴿and reform﴾ themselves through faith and righteous deeds, ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. This is like a promise from Him, glorified and exalted, that He will forgive them their sins and have mercy on them by admitting them into Paradise.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Persisting in evil and corruption, or in wrongdoing and disbelief, may prevent the servant from repentance. Therefore, when a servant commits a sin, he must repent from it immediately and not continue in it persistently, lest he be prevented from repenting.

2. Repentance is accepted when it stands on its foundations and fulfils its conditions, among which are: ceasing the sin immediately, regret for having committed it, seeking forgiveness, resolving not to return to the sin repented of, and amending what has been corrupted, where amendment is possible.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 90–91:

Explanation of the words:

Al-kufr (disbelief): denial of Allah Most High and rejection of His Messenger and of the religion and law he brought.

Ba'da imanihim (after their faith): that is, they apostatized from Islam into disbelief.

Al-dallun (those who go astray): those who miss the path of guidance.

Mil' al-ard (the filling of the earth): what would fill it of gold.

Wa law iftada bihi (even if he offered it as ransom): even if he offered it as a ransom for himself from the Fire, it would not be accepted from him.

Meaning of the two verses:

The context still concerns the People of the Book, specifically the Jews. Allah Most High informs us about them that they disbelieved after their faith: they disbelieved in Jesus and the Injil after their faith in Moses and the Torah, and they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. Their repentance will not be accepted unless they repent by believing in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, but they are persistent in disbelief in both. How, then, could their repentance be accepted while they persist in disbelief? For this reason Allah Most High informs us that they are the ones who go astray, reaching the furthest limits of error, and whoever is in this state does not repent, and his repentance is not accepted. Then He established their final destiny by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, never will be accepted from any of them the filling of the earth in gold﴾. He means the Day of Resurrection, even though there will be no wealth on that day, but this is merely by way of supposition and assumption. So even if one of them had the filling of the earth in gold and it were accepted from him as a ransom for himself from the punishment of Allah, he would offer it. But far, far away is that; it is a day on which neither wealth nor children will benefit, but whoever comes to his Lord with a sound heart, free from polytheism, doubt and all other diseases of the heart, will be saved from the Fire and enter Paradise by the permission of Allah Most High.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- Allah's way with those who plunge deeply into disbelief, wrongdoing or sin, and reach an extreme limit, is that they do not repent.

2- Despair of salvation for those who die in disbelief on the Day of Resurrection.

3- No ransom will be accepted on the Day of Resurrection from anyone, and no redemption for anyone will be made through it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verse 92:

Explanation of the words:

Lan tanalu (لن تنالوا): lan tuhsilu alayhi wa tazfaru bihi (you will not obtain it and attain it).

Al-birr (البرّ): a comprehensive word for every good; what is meant here is its reward, which is Paradise.

Tunfiqu (تنفقوا): tatasaddaqu (you give in charity).

Mimma tuhibbun (مما تحبون): from the wealth that you love for yourselves, which is the best of your wealth in your estimation.

Min shay' (من شيء): meaning, whether little or much.

Fa-inna Allaha bihi alim (فإن الله به عليم): its implication is that He will reward you for it according to its abundance or scarcity.

Meaning of the noble verse:

He, exalted is He, informs His believing servants, who desire His righteousness and bounty, that by His saving them from the Fire and admitting them into Paradise, they will not attain their goal of His righteousness until they spend from their finest wealth, the most precious to them and the dearest to them. Then He informed them, reassuring them regarding their spending of their best wealth, that whatever they spend, whether little or much, precious or base, He knows it and will reward them for it. With this, He made spending beloved to them and encouraged them to it. Abu Talha, may Allah be pleased with him, came saying: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love﴾, and indeed among my most beloved wealth to me is Bayruha' (a garden). So place it where Allah shows you, O Messenger of Allah." He (ﷺ) said to him: "That is profitable wealth (mal rabih) or (mal rai'ij); place it among your relatives." So he placed it among his relatives, Hassan ibn Thabit and Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Guidance of the verse

From the guidance of the verse:

1- Righteousness, which is the doing of good, leads to Paradise.

2- A servant will not reach the righteousness of Allah and what He has of the bounties of the Hereafter until he spends of his most beloved wealth.

3- Good deeds are not lost with Allah, whether small or great, so long as they are done seeking His countenance.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 93–97:

Explanation of the words:

Al-ta'am (food): a name for everything that is eaten, of all kinds of foodstuffs.

Hill (lawful): al-hill means al-halal (the lawful), and it was so called because the knot of prohibition is untied from it (inhilal).

Banu Isra'il (Children of Israel): the descendants of Ya'qub, who is called Isra'il, from his twelve sons, down to our day.

Harrama (forbade): prohibited and prevented.

Al-Tawrat (the Torah): the Book revealed to Musa, peace be upon him, who was of the progeny of Isra'il.

Fa'tluha (then recite it): read it openly before the assembly, so that we may distinguish the truth of your claim from its falsehood.

Iftara al-kadhib (fabricated the lie): invented it, forged it and said it.

Millat Ibrahim (the creed of Ibrahim): his religion, which is the worship of Allah the Exalted in the manner He has prescribed, and the rejection of polytheism and innovations.

Hanifan (upright): turning away from polytheism toward monotheism.

Bakka: Makkah.

Lil-'alamin (for all of mankind): for all people.

Maqam Ibrahim (the Station of Ibrahim): one of the signs, namely the stone on which he stood during the building of the House, whereupon his feet left their imprint. It is a rock, and this was a sign.

Man dakhalahu (whoever enters it): the Sanctuary (al-Haram) surrounding the House within its well-known boundaries.

Aminan (secure): not fearing for life, property or honour.

Al-hajj (the pilgrimage): intending the House to circumambulate it and perform the remaining rites.

Sabilan (a way/means): a way; what is meant is the ability to travel to the House and to perform the rites.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues in the argument with the People of the Book. The Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: "How do you claim to be upon the religion of Ibrahim while you eat what is forbidden in his religion, such as the flesh of camels and their milk?" Allah the Exalted refuted this false claim by saying: "All food was lawful (hillan) for the Children of Israel, who are the descendants of Ya'qub, called Isra'il, and there was nothing forbidden to them in the religion of Ibrahim, except what Isra'il (Ya'qub) forbade to himself personally, namely the flesh of camels and their milk, by way of a vow he made: he fell ill with an illness that pained him, so he vowed to Allah that if He cured him he would forsake the food and drink he loved most, and the flesh and milk of camels were among the foods and drinks he loved most, so he abstained from them for the sake of Allah." This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿All food was lawful for the Children of Israel, except what Isra'il forbade to himself﴾, before the Torah was sent down, since the Torah was revealed to Musa many generations after Ibrahim and Ya'qub. So how can you claim that Ibrahim did not eat the flesh of camels or drink their milk? Bring the Torah and recite it, and you will find that what Allah forbade to the Jews was only because of their wrongdoing and transgression; He forbade them various kinds of food, and that was many generations after Ibrahim and Ya'qub. Allah said in Surah al-Nisa': ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things that had been lawful for them﴾ [v. 160] (the Jews), and He said in Surah al-An'am: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws, and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat﴾ [v. 146].

When they were challenged to bring the Torah and read it, they were confounded and did not do so, and thus the proof was established against them for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. As for His words: ﴿Then whoever fabricates a lie against Allah after this﴾, after the proof had been established that Allah had not forbidden to Ibrahim or to the Children of Israel any food or drink until after the Torah was sent down, except what Isra'il forbade to himself of the flesh of camels and their milk, "then they are the wrongdoers" in lying against Allah and against the people.

From here Allah commanded His Messenger to say: ﴿Allah has spoken the truth﴾ concerning what He informed His Messenger and will inform him, for it is the truth from Allah. ﴿So follow the creed of Ibrahim, upright, and he was not of the polytheists﴾, O company of Jews.

This is what the three verses 93, 94 and 95 contain. As for His words: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾, it contains a refutation of the Jews who said that Bayt al-Maqdis was the first qibla legislated for people to face, so why would Muhammad and his companions turn away from it toward facing the Ka'bah, which came later in existence? Allah the Exalted informed them that the first House established for mankind is the Ka'bah, not Bayt al-Maqdis, and that He made it blessed, enduring as long as the world endures; blessing never departs from it, so whoever seeks it by visiting it, performing hajj and circumambulating it will find it and attain it. He also made it a guidance for the worlds: believers come as pilgrims and visitors, and various kinds of guidance are thereby obtained for them, and those who pray in the east and west of the earth face it in their prayers. Among the guidance it provides is obtaining reward, remembrance of Allah and drawing near to Him, which is the greatest guidance. His words ﴿in it are clear signs﴾ mean: in the Sacred Mosque are manifest proofs, among them the Station of Ibrahim, the stone on which he stood during the building of the House, where the mark of his two feet remained upon it although it is a rock among rocks; and among them the Zamzam well, al-Hijr, al-Safa and al-Marwah, and all the sacred places are signs. Among them also is the complete security of whoever enters it, so that he fears none but Allah. Allah said: ﴿And whoever enters it is secure﴾. This security is granted even though the Arabs lived in utter ignorance and unbridled chaos without limit, yet Allah placed in their hearts reverence for the Sanctuary and its sanctity, and the obligation to secure everyone who enters it to perform hajj or 'umrah.

His words ﴿And due to Allah from the people is pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find thereto a way﴾: when Allah mentioned the Sacred House and the blessings, guidance and signs in it, He obligated His servants who believe in Him and His Messenger to make pilgrimage to it, so that good, blessing and guidance might be attained by them. He made it obligatory with the expression "due to Allah from the people," which is the most emphatic form of obligation, and He excepted those unable to perform hajj or 'umrah due to illness, fear, or lack of means for transport and for supporting themselves and their families during the journey.

Allah the Exalted informed them that the first House established for mankind is the Ka'bah, not Bayt al-Maqdis, and that He made it blessed, enduring as long as the world endures; blessing never departs from it, so whoever seeks it by visiting it, performing hajj and circumambulating it will find it and attain it. He also made it a guidance for the worlds: believers come as pilgrims and visitors, and various kinds of guidance are thereby obtained for them, and those who pray in the east and west of the earth face it in their prayers. Among the guidance it provides is obtaining reward, remembrance of Allah and drawing near to Him, which is the greatest guidance. His words ﴿in it are clear signs﴾ mean: in the Sacred Mosque are manifest proofs, among them the Station of Ibrahim, the stone on which he stood during the building of the House, where the mark of his two feet remained upon it although it is a rock among rocks; and among them the Zamzam well, al-Hijr, al-Safa and al-Marwah, and all the sacred places are signs. Among them also is the complete security of whoever enters it, so that he fears none but Allah. Allah said: ﴿And whoever enters it is secure﴾. This security is granted even though the Arabs lived in utter ignorance and unbridled chaos without limit, yet Allah placed in their hearts reverence for the Sanctuary and its sanctity, and the obligation to secure everyone who enters it to perform hajj or 'umrah.

His words ﴿And due to Allah from the people is pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find thereto a way﴾: when Allah mentioned the Sacred House and the blessings, guidance and signs in it, He obligated His servants who believe in Him and His Messenger to make pilgrimage to it, so that good, blessing and guidance might be attained by them. He made it obligatory with the expression "due to Allah from the people," which is the most emphatic form of obligation, and He excepted those unable to perform hajj or 'umrah due to illness, fear, or lack of means for transport and for supporting themselves and their families during the journey.

His words at the end of the verse: ﴿And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾ are a statement from Him that whoever disbelieves in Allah and His Messenger and does not make pilgrimage to His House after the signs and clear proofs mentioned, then he harms no one but himself; Allah is not harmed by anything. How could He be, when He is the Irresistible above His servants and free of need from all of them?

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- The establishment of abrogation (naskh) in divine laws, since Allah forbade the Jews some things that had been lawful to them.

2- The refutation of the Jews' claim that Ibrahim had forbidden himself the flesh of camels and their milk.

3- The affirmation of Muhammadan prophethood through challenging the Jews, and their inability to refute the truth brought by Muhammad ﷺ.

4- The Sacred House existed before Bayt al-Maqdis, and the Sacred House is the first house established for worship by circumambulating it.

5- The legitimacy of seeking blessing by visiting the House, performing hajj to it, circumambulating it and worshipping around it.

6- The obligation of hajj immediately for whoever has no impediment preventing him from it.

7- An indication of the disbelief of whoever abandons hajj while able to perform it, with no obstacle preventing him other than indifference.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 98–99:

Explanation of the words:

Al-kufr (disbelief): denial (al-juhud).

Ayat Allah (the signs of Allah): what Allah, exalted is He, has sent down of proofs and clear evidences in the Qur'an establishing the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and what He has sent down in the Torah and the Gospel of the attributes and descriptions of the Prophet (ﷺ) that necessitate belief in him and following him in the religion of truth that he brought, which is Islam.

Shahid ala ma ta'malun (a witness over what you do): All-Knowing of it, observing it; and [He is observing] what they do, which is disbelief, evil and corruption.

Tasuddun 'an sabil Allah (you bar from the way of Allah): you turn people away, from among those of you who have believed and from among the Arabs, from Islam, which is the way of Allah exalted, the way that leads its people to the happiness of both abodes.

Tabghunaha 'iwajan (you seek to make it crooked): you seek crookedness in it, so that you may take it out of the truth and guidance, and the one who follows it goes astray; this is by distortion and misleading.

Wa antum shuhada' (while you are witnesses): by your knowledge that Islam is true, and that what you seek for it of misguiding its people and deception is disbelief and falsehood.

Meaning of the two verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, refuted and nullified the doubts of the People of the Book in the preceding verses, He commanded His Messenger to say to them, rebuking them and recording their disbelief: "O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the proofs of Allah and His evidences that establish the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his religion, Islam, those proofs and evidences that the Qur'an, the Torah and the Gospel have brought together?" And Allah, majestic is His majesty, is observant of your disbelief and knows it. Do you not fear His punishment? Do you not dread His torment?

He also commanded His Messenger to say to them, reproaching and rebuking them for turning the believers away from Islam by various kinds of tricks and deception: "O People of the Book, that is, O people of the earliest knowledge, why do you turn the believers away from Islam, which is the way of Allah, by the doubts and illusions you stir up among them, seeking crookedness in Islam so that the believers will turn away from it, while you have complete knowledge of the soundness of Islam and the truthfulness of its Prophet Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him? Do you not fear Allah? Do you not dread Him, exalted is He, while He observes the evil of your scheming, and is not unaware of your cunning, deceit and treachery?"

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The extreme ugliness of the disbelief and wrongdoing of those among the People of the Book who had knowledge of the truth and then disbelieved in it and denied it out of rebellion and envy.

2- The prohibition of turning people away from truth and righteousness by various kinds of tricks and forms of lying and deception.

3- Allah, exalted is He, knows all the deeds of His servants, good and evil, and will recompense them for them, by His grace and justice.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 100–103:

Explanation of the words:

Firqan (a group): a party among those who harbour enmity toward Islam, working to plot against it and deceive it and its people.

Yaruddukum (they would turn you back): they would cause you to return to disbelief after your belief.

Wa kayfa takfuruna (And how could you disbelieve?): the interrogative is one of denunciation and astonishment at their disbelief after their belief.

Ayat Allah (the signs of Allah): the verses of the Noble Qur'an.

Ya'tasimu (holds fast): clings firmly.

Haqqa tuqatihi (as He truly deserves to be feared): by exerting one's utmost effort in carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions; taqatihi is His taqwa (God-consciousness).

Habl Allah (the rope of Allah): His Book, the Qur'an, and His religion, Islam, because the Book and the religion are the link that connects the Muslim to his Lord; and everything that binds and fastens one thing to another is a cause and a rope (habl).

Allafa bayna qulubikum (He joined your hearts): He gathered them in the brotherhood of faith and united them after disagreement and aversion.

Shafa hufrah (the brink of a pit): the brink of the pit and its edge, such that whoever stands on it heedlessly will fall into it.

Anqadhakum minha (He rescued you from it): by guiding you to Islam, and thereby saving you from the Fire.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, rebuked the Jews for their deception, their scheming and their misguidance of the believers, and threatened them for it, He addressed the believers, warning them against falling into the snares of the misguiding Jews, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you after your belief to disbelief﴾. This was because a group of the Aws and the Khazraj were sitting in an assembly where affection and purity of heart prevailed, by the blessing of Islam, through which Allah had guided them. Shas ibn Qays, a Jew, passed by them; that harmony and mutual love pained him and grieved him, since the Jews had been living in security from fear of their neighbours, the Aws and the Khazraj, because of the destruction and ruin that had existed between them. So Shas ordered a young man to remind them of the Day of Bu'ath, and they recalled it and recited poetry to one another. Tribal zeal then flared up among them; they reviled and insulted one another until they were about to fight. The Messenger ﷺ came to them and reminded them of Allah and of his own station among them, and they calmed down, and the evil departed. Then these verses were revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you after your belief to disbelief﴾. So He warned them against the scheming of the deceivers among the Jews and the Christians, and denounced what had happened from them, prompting them to marvel at their condition: if they were to disbelieve after their belief. He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And how could you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you morning and evening in the prayers and otherwise, and among you is His Messenger as a guide, a bringer of good tidings and a warner?﴾ He guided them to hold fast to the religion of Allah, and gave good tidings to those who hold fast of guidance to the path of happiness and perfection, saying: ﴿And whoever holds fast to Allah, that is, to His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet, has indeed been guided to a straight path.﴾ Then Allah, exalted is He, repeated His address to them under the title of faith, to remind them of it, and commanded them to exert their utmost effort in the taqwa of Allah, mighty and majestic, namely by obeying Him with complete obedience, carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibition, urging them to remain steadfast upon the religion of Allah until they die upon it, neither altering nor changing it, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He truly deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.﴾ He commanded them to hold fast to Islam in creed and law, forbade them from division and disagreement, and directed them to remember His blessing upon them in the harmony and love that was the fruit of their guidance to faith and Islam. Having been enemies, hostile and divided, He joined their hearts, so that by it they became brothers, loving and cooperating. And they were, by the blessing of guidance to faith, on the brink of the pit of Hell: had one of them died at that time, he would have fallen into it forever. Just as He bestowed His blessing upon them and rescued them from the Fire, He continues to make clear to them the signs that indicate the path of guidance and call to it, so as to keep them firm in guidance and perfect them in it. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah, and do not be divided. And remember the blessing of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He joined your hearts, so that by His blessing you became brothers; and you were on the brink of a pit of the Fire and He rescued you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs, that you may be guided.﴾

Lessons from the verses:

1- Obeying many of the scholars of the Jews and the Christians, by taking their advice and guidance and what they point out to the Muslim, leads the Muslim to disbelief, whether he perceives it or not; therefore it is obligatory to be wary, with the utmost caution, of them.

2- Security lies in holding fast to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; whoever holds fast to both will not go astray.

3- Taking up Islam wholly and holding fast to it in creed and law is a safeguard from deviation and misguidance, and ultimately from ruin and loss.

4- It is obligatory to hold firmly to the Islamic religion, and division and disagreement within it are forbidden.

5- It is obligatory to mention blessings in order to thank Allah for them by obeying Him and His Messenger ﷺ.

6- Persisting in shirk and sins is standing on the edge of Hell; whoever dies in that state will certainly fall into Hell, by the decree and judgment of Allah.

He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And how could you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you morning and evening in the prayers and otherwise, and among you is His Messenger as a guide, a bringer of good tidings and a warner?﴾ He guided them to hold fast to the religion of Allah, and gave good tidings to those who hold fast of guidance to the path of happiness and perfection, saying: ﴿And whoever holds fast to Allah, that is, to His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet, has indeed been guided to a straight path.﴾ Then Allah, exalted is He, repeated His address to them under the title of faith, to remind them of it, and commanded them to exert their utmost effort in the taqwa of Allah, mighty and majestic, namely by obeying Him with complete obedience, carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibition, urging them to remain steadfast upon the religion of Allah until they die upon it, neither altering nor changing it, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He truly deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.﴾ He commanded them to hold fast to Islam in creed and law, forbade them from division and disagreement, and directed them to remember His blessing upon them in the harmony and love that was the fruit of their guidance to faith and Islam. Having been enemies, hostile and divided, He joined their hearts, so that by it they became brothers, loving and cooperating. And they were, by the blessing of guidance to faith, on the brink of the pit of Hell: had one of them died at that time, he would have fallen into it forever. Just as He bestowed His blessing upon them and rescued them from the Fire, He continues to make clear to them the signs that indicate the path of guidance and call to it, so as to keep them firm in guidance and perfect them in it. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah, and do not be divided. And remember the blessing of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He joined your hearts, so that by His blessing you became brothers; and you were on the brink of a pit of the Fire and He rescued you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs, that you may be guided.﴾

Lessons from the verses:

1- Obeying many of the scholars of the Jews and the Christians, by taking their advice and guidance and what they point out to the Muslim, leads the Muslim to disbelief, whether he perceives it or not; therefore it is obligatory to be wary, with the utmost caution, of them.

2- Security lies in holding fast to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; whoever holds fast to both will not go astray.

3- Taking up Islam wholly and holding fast to it in creed and law is a safeguard from deviation and misguidance, and ultimately from ruin and loss.

4- It is obligatory to hold firmly to the Islamic religion, and division and disagreement within it are forbidden.

5- It is obligatory to mention blessings in order to thank Allah for them by obeying Him and His Messenger ﷺ.

6- Persisting in shirk and sins is standing on the edge of Hell; whoever dies in that state will certainly fall into Hell, by the decree and judgment of Allah.

Khayr (good): Islam, and everything that benefits a person in this life and the next, from faith and righteous deeds.

Ma'ruf (what is good/known): whatever the Sharia has recognized and commanded for its benefit and well-being for the individual or the community.

Munkar (what is evil/disavowed): the opposite of ma'ruf, namely what the Sharia has forbidden for its harm and corruption, to the individual or the community.

Those who divided (alladhina tafarraqu): these are the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians.

The day when faces will turn white (yawma tabyaddu wujuh): this is the Day of Resurrection.

Then in the mercy of God (fa-fi rahmati Allah): the mercy of God here is Paradise; may God make us among its people, amin.

Those are the signs of God which We recite to you in truth: these are Our signs which We recite to you, coupled with truth, never with falsehood.

And to God are all matters returned: all matters will be referred to God, who will judge in them as He wills and decree as He desires, out of bounty and justice.

Explanation of the verses:

After the Exalted and Blessed God commanded His believing servants to be mindful of Him and to hold fast to His religion, and forbade them from division and disagreement, and urged them to remember His blessings so that they would thank Him by obeying Him, He commanded them in this verse [104] to bring into being from among themselves a community that calls to Islam, by presenting it to the nations and peoples and inviting them to enter it, and that enjoins good and forbids evil within the lands of Islam and among its people. So He said, addressing them: "And let there be [arising] from you a community who invite to good," that is, there must be among you a group who call to good, that is Islam, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. He gave them the good news that the community that rises to this duty is the one that attains the happiness of this world and the next, so He said: "Those are the successful," those who attain deliverance from shame and the Fire and entry into Paradise with the righteous.

In verses [105] [106] [107], He forbade them to follow the path of the People of the Book in division over affairs and disagreement in religion, lest they perish as they perished. So the Exalted said, addressing them: "And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them." It is not fitting that knowledge and understanding of God's laws should be a cause of division and dispute, when they are the means of unity and harmony. He informed them of the recompense of the disputing People of the Book so that they would take heed and not differ or divide, so He said: "And for those is a great punishment," which none can measure in its extent nor know its limit. He informed them of the appointed time when this great punishment would befall them: it is the Day of Resurrection, when the faces of the believers who are united and who uphold the Book and the Sunnah will become white, and the faces of the disbelievers who are divided and who adhere to innovations and whims will become black. So the Exalted said: "On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black." He explained the recompense of the two groups, saying: "As for those whose faces turned black, [it will be said to them]: 'Did you disbelieve after your belief? Taste, then, the punishment for what you used to deny.'" Their faces will be blackened from the evil of what they witnessed of the terrors of the standing place and from their certainty that they are headed to the torment of the Fire. It will be said to them in rebuke and reproach: "Did you disbelieve after your faith?" For these are faces belonging to those in such a state. "Taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve in God and His laws."

As for those whose faces turned white, their standing in terror will not be prolonged before they enter the Paradise of their Lord. The Exalted said: "So they will be in the mercy of God, abiding therein forever."

In verse [108], God honored His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ by addressing him and revealing to him, so He said: "These are the signs of God which We recite to you in truth," that is, these signs, containing guidance and good, We recite to you in the established truth about which there is no doubt and no uncertainty reaches it. So convey them from Us and call people to them by them; whoever responds to you is saved, and whoever turns away is ruined. "And God does not want injustice for the worlds," so He does not punish except after information and warning.

In the final verse [109], the Exalted informs that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth in creation, disposition and management, and that the final outcome of affairs is to Him, and that He will recompense the doer of good with the best and the doer of evil with the worst.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation that there be a group within the community of Islam calling the nations and peoples to Islam, presenting it to them, and fighting them if they fight it; and the obligation that there be bodies enjoining good and forbidding evil in every city and village of the Muslims.

2- The prohibition of division among Muslims and of disagreement in the religion of God.

3- The people of innovation and whims will be recognized on the plains of Resurrection by the blackness of their faces.

4- The people of the Sunnah and the community, who live by the creed and worship upheld by the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions, will be recognized on the Day of Gathering by the whiteness of their faces.

5- The honor of the Messenger with his Lord and the affirmation of his prophethood, and the nobility of those who believe in him and follow what he brought.

6- The return of all affairs to God in this world and the next; therefore, it is incumbent upon wise servants to make for themselves a covenant with God by believing in Him and affirming His unity in worship, by realizing "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God" ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 104–109:

Explanation of the words:

Ummah (community): individuals of humankind or others bound together by a common lineage, language or religion, and whose affair is one. The intended meaning here is those who strive in the cause of God and the bodies that enjoin good and forbid evil.

Khayr (good): Islam, and everything that benefits a person in this life and the next, from faith and righteous deeds.

Ma'ruf (what is good/known): whatever the Sharia has recognized and commanded for its benefit and well-being for the individual or the community.

Munkar (what is evil/disavowed): the opposite of ma'ruf, namely what the Sharia has forbidden for its harm and corruption, to the individual or the community.

Those who divided (alladhina tafarraqu): these are the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians.

The day when faces will turn white (yawma tabyaddu wujuh): this is the Day of Resurrection.

Then in the mercy of God (fa-fi rahmati Allah): the mercy of God here is Paradise; may God make us among its people, amin.

Those are the signs of God which We recite to you in truth: these are Our signs which We recite to you, coupled with truth, never with falsehood.

And to God are all matters returned: all matters will be referred to God, who will judge in them as He wills and decree as He desires, out of bounty and justice.

Explanation of the verses:

After the Exalted and Blessed God commanded His believing servants to be mindful of Him and to hold fast to His religion, and forbade them from division and disagreement, and urged them to remember His blessings so that they would thank Him by obeying Him, He commanded them in this verse [104] to bring into being from among themselves a community that calls to Islam, by presenting it to the nations and peoples and inviting them to enter it, and that enjoins good and forbids evil within the lands of Islam and among its people. So He said, addressing them: "And let there be [arising] from you a community who invite to good," that is, there must be among you a group who call to good, that is Islam, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. He gave them the good news that the community that rises to this duty is the one that attains the happiness of this world and the next, so He said: "Those are the successful," those who attain deliverance from shame and the Fire and entry into Paradise with the righteous.

In verses [105] [106] [107], He forbade them to follow the path of the People of the Book in division over affairs and disagreement in religion, lest they perish as they perished. So the Exalted said, addressing them: "And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them." It is not fitting that knowledge and understanding of God's laws should be a cause of division and dispute, when they are the means of unity and harmony. He informed them of the recompense of the disputing People of the Book so that they would take heed and not differ or divide, so He said: "And for those is a great punishment," which none can measure in its extent nor know its limit. He informed them of the appointed time when this great punishment would befall them: it is the Day of Resurrection, when the faces of the believers who are united and who uphold the Book and the Sunnah will become white, and the faces of the disbelievers who are divided and who adhere to innovations and whims will become black. So the Exalted said: "On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black." He explained the recompense of the two groups, saying: "As for those whose faces turned black, [it will be said to them]: 'Did you disbelieve after your belief? Taste, then, the punishment for what you used to deny.'" Their faces will be blackened from the evil of what they witnessed of the terrors of the standing place and from their certainty that they are headed to the torment of the Fire. It will be said to them in rebuke and reproach: "Did you disbelieve after your faith?" For these are faces belonging to those in such a state. "Taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve in God and His laws."

As for those whose faces turned white, their standing in terror will not be prolonged before they enter the Paradise of their Lord. The Exalted said: "So they will be in the mercy of God, abiding therein forever."

In verse [108], God honored His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ by addressing him and revealing to him, so He said: "These are the signs of God which We recite to you in truth," that is, these signs, containing guidance and good, We recite to you in the established truth about which there is no doubt and no uncertainty reaches it. So convey them from Us and call people to them by them; whoever responds to you is saved, and whoever turns away is ruined. "And God does not want injustice for the worlds," so He does not punish except after information and warning.

In the final verse [109], the Exalted informs that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth in creation, disposition and management, and that the final outcome of affairs is to Him, and that He will recompense the doer of good with the best and the doer of evil with the worst.
