2- The prohibition of division among Muslims and of disagreement in the religion of God.

3- The people of innovation and whims will be recognized on the plains of Resurrection by the blackness of their faces.

4- The people of the Sunnah and the community, who live by the creed and worship upheld by the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions, will be recognized on the Day of Gathering by the whiteness of their faces.

5- The honor of the Messenger with his Lord and the affirmation of his prophethood, and the nobility of those who believe in him and follow what he brought.

6- The return of all affairs to God in this world and the next; therefore, it is incumbent upon wise servants to make for themselves a covenant with God by believing in Him and affirming His unity in worship, by realizing "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God" ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 110–112:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Kuntum khayra ummah﴾ (You were the best nation): You were found to be the most excellent and most blessed nation ever to exist on earth.

﴿Ukhrijat lil-nas﴾ (brought forth for mankind): Made manifest and brought out for the guidance and benefit of mankind.

Adha (harm): Adha is slight harm.

﴿Yuwallukum al-adbar﴾ (they will turn their backs to you): They will be defeated and flee from the battle, turning their backs to you, i.e., their backs.

﴿Duribat 'alayhim al-dhillah﴾ (humiliation was imposed upon them): Humiliation surrounded them and clung to them so that it never leaves them.

﴿Wa-ba'u bi-ghadabin﴾ (and they returned with wrath): They returned from their long journey in disbelief and doing evil, with the wrath of Allah.

﴿Dhalika bi-annahum...﴾ etc.: "Dhalika" refers to what clung to them of humiliation and destitution, and what they incurred of the wrath of Allah the Exalted and the punishment that followed it. The "ba'" in "bi-annahum" is causal, meaning because of their doing such and such. Al-maskanah is the humiliation of poverty and need.

﴿Ya'tadun﴾ (they transgress): Transgression is exceeding the limit in wrongdoing, evil and corruption.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah the Exalted commanded the believers to fear Him and to hold fast to His rope, and they complied, and He commanded them to form a group among themselves that calls to Islam and enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong, and they complied, He mentioned them with great goodness, saying to them: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "You are the best of people for people..." He described them with what made them the best nation, saying: "You enjoin what is right", which is Islam and the laws of guidance that his Prophet ﷺ brought; "and forbid what is wrong", which is disbelief, polytheism, major sins and indecencies; "and believe in Allah", and with what belief in Allah entails of believing in everything He commanded belief in: the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Resurrection and divine decree. Then the Exalted called the People of the Book to true faith that saves from the punishment of Allah, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them﴾, meaning, if the People of the Book had believed in the Prophet Muhammad and what he brought of Islam, it would have been better for them than the false claim of faith that they make. And Allah the Exalted informed that among them are sincere believers in their faith, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and his brother, and Tha'labah ibn Sa'id and his brother; but most of them are defiant transgressors who did not act upon what came in their scripture of beliefs and laws, including the command of Allah the Exalted to believe in the unlettered Prophet and follow him in what he brings of Islam. Then He informed the Muslims that the wicked among the People of the Book will not harm them except with slight harm, such as their hearing of falsehood and their lying speech. And that if they fight them, they will turn their backs, fleeing from the battle, and then they will not be victorious over the Muslims in any battle that takes place between the two sides.

As Allah the Exalted informed in verse [112] that He imposed upon them humiliation and destitution wherever they are found and in whatever lands they are met; humiliation and destitution will never leave them in any circumstance, except when they enter Islam, which is the rope of Allah, or a covenant and bond with a strong state, and that is the rope of people. He also informed that they returned from their obstinacy and disbelief with wrath from Allah, and what follows it of punishment in this world, in the state of need and poverty expressed by al-maskanah, and in the Hereafter, with the punishment of Hell. He also mentioned the cause of their punishment, which is disbelief in the signs of Allah, the killing of the prophets without right, their persistent disobedience and their unceasing transgression, when He the Exalted said: ﴿That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.﴾

Guidance from the verses:

1. Affirmation of the excellence of the Muslim nation; and in the hadith: "You complete seventy nations, you are the best of them and the most honored of them before Allah."
2. Explanation of the cause of the excellence of the Muslim nation, which is faith in Allah, jihad, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong.
3. Allah's promise to the Muslim nation, so long as it holds fast to this, of victory over the Jews in any battle that takes place between them.
4. The truthfulness of the Qur'an in its report about the Jews, that humiliation and destitution cling to them wherever they are.
5. Explanation of the crimes of the Jews that were the cause of their humiliation and destitution: continuous disbelief, killing the prophets without right, disobedience, and transgression against the limits of the Sharia.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 113–115:

Explanation of the words:

Laysu sawa': not equal.

Ummah qa'imah: an upright, steadfast community, firm in faith and righteous deeds.

Yatluna ayat Allah: they recite the Qur'an.

Ana'a al-layl: the hours of the night (plural of ini, and ini).

Wa hum yasjudun: they pray.

Yusari'una fi al-khayrat: they hasten to good deeds, racing to seize them lest they be missed.

Fa-lan yukfarūhu: they will not be denied it; rather, it will be acknowledged for them and they will be rewarded for it in full.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the condition of the People of the Book, that they are of two groups, a righteous believing group and a corrupt disbelieving group, He mentions here in these three verses [113, 114, 115] that the People of the Book are not all alike, that is, not equal in condition, and He praises the righteous among them, saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿They are not all alike. Among the People of the Book is an upright community﴾, meaning steadfast upon true faith and the correct religion, and they are those who embraced Islam. ﴿They recite the verses of Allah during the night hours﴾, meaning in their prayers during the hours of the night, in the night prayer and voluntary night vigil. ﴿And they prostrate themselves﴾, and this is a praise of them for prostration, as it is the greatest manifestation of submission to Allah, exalted is He, just as He praised them for sincere faith, for enjoining what is good, which is calling to the worship of Allah after believing in Him, and for outward and inward Islam submitted to Him. ﴿And they forbid what is wrong﴾, which is associating partners with Allah in worship and disbelieving in Him and in His Messenger. Then He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they hasten to good deeds﴾, meaning they hurry to them before they are missed, and the good deeds are every good word and deed from among all acts of devotion. Allah, exalted is He, bore witness to their righteousness, saying: ﴿And those are among the righteous﴾.

Finally, in the last verse [115], what they do of righteous deeds and good works will not be denied; rather, it will be acknowledged for them and they will be rewarded for it in the fullest measure, because they are God-fearing, and Allah is All-Knowing of the God-fearing, so their reward will not be lost.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The virtue of steadfastness upon the truth and persistence in acts of obedience.

2- The virtue of reciting the Noble Qur'an in the night prayer.

3- The virtue of faith and of calling to Islam.

4- The virtue of racing toward good deeds and hastening to righteous acts.

5- The excellence of the People of the Book when they embrace Islam and their Islam is sound. In the Two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and then encountered the Prophet (ﷺ), believed in him, followed him and affirmed him, he will have two rewards..." [the hadith].

In the Two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and then encountered the Prophet (ﷺ), believed in him, followed him and affirmed him, he will have two rewards..." [the hadith].

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Kafaru* (كفروا): they denied Allah, His Messenger, His law, and His religion.

*Lan tughni 'anhum* (لن تغني عنهم): their wealth will not avail them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will their children, against the punishment of Allah in any way, since no wealth or sons will benefit anyone on that Day.

*Mathal* (مثل): the description and condition of what they spend, whether to obstruct the call of Islam or to give in charity.

*Al-Sirr* (الصرّ): a cold wind of severe cold that kills and ruins crops.

*Al-Harth* (الحرث): that for which the land is ploughed, namely the crop.

*Zalamu anfusahum* (ظلموا أنفسهم): they defiled themselves with polytheism and sins, thereby exposing themselves to destruction and loss.

**The Meaning of the Two Verses:**

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the condition of the believers among the People of the Book and praised them for the perfect qualities He had bestowed upon them, He mentioned here, in these two verses, what He threatened for the disbelievers of the two scriptures and for the other polytheists, following the Qur'anic method of encouragement and warning, so that whoever Allah has prepared for guidance may be guided. This is what the first verse contains [116].

Allah said: ﴿And Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾.

1- Wealth and children will not avail a person when he wrongs himself and exposes himself to the vengeance of Allah, the Exalted.

2- The people of disbelief are the people of the Fire, and their eternal abiding therein is a decreed judgment upon them, from which there is no escape.

3- The nullification of righteous deeds through polytheism and dying in disbelief.

4- The commendability of using parables in speech to bring meanings closer to minds.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 118–120:

Explanation of the words:

Bitanah (intimate confidants): the intimates of a man, who are made aware of the inner affairs of his matters that he hides from people for the sake of interest.

Min dunikum (from other than you): from others than you, i.e., from non-Muslims such as the disbelievers and the People of the Book.

La ya'lunakum (they do not fall short of you): they do not fall short in corrupting matters for you.

Khabalan (corruption): corruption in the affairs of your religion and your worldly life.

Waddu ma 'anittum (they love your distress): they love your suffering, i.e., your hardship.

Badat al-baghda' (hatred has appeared): the intensity of their hatred for you has become manifest.

Ula' (these): "hā'ulā'," from which the particle of alerting (hā') has been dropped because it is present in "hā antum" before it.

Bil-kitab kullihi (in the whole Book): i.e., in all the divine scriptures.

'Addu 'alaykumu al-anamil min al-ghayz (they bite their fingertips out of rage at you): out of intense anger against you, because the one who is enraged, when his rage becomes intense, bites his finger, as is the habit of human beings. Al-ghayz is the intensity of anger.

Hasanah (a good thing): whatever is good of kinds of benefit, such as victory, support, strength and goodness.

Sayyi'ah (a bad thing): whatever displeases you, such as defeat, death or famine.

Kaydahum (their scheming): their plotting against you and their devising of evil for you.

Bima ya'malun muhit (what they do is encompassed): He has knowledge of it and power over it, since they are under His subjugation and His great dominion.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, informed about the fate of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, and that this dark fate was the result of their disbelief and wrongdoing, He warned the believers against allying themselves with them instead of with the believers, especially those who carry in their breasts rage and hatred toward the Muslims, who do not fall short in working to corrupt the condition of the Muslims, and who are displeased to see the Muslims united, loving one another, strong, prevailing and victorious over the people of polytheism and disbelief, and who are likewise delighted to see the Muslims divided, weak, broken and defeated. So Allah the Exalted said — and His word is the truth — "O you who have believed" — that is, who believe in Allah as Lord, in Islam as religion, and in Muhammad (ﷺ) as Prophet and Messenger.

"Do not take intimate confidants" — that is, individuals from other than you, i.e., from outside your religion, such as the Jews, the Christians, the hypocrites and the polytheists, whom you consult and to whom you disclose your secrets and the inner affairs of your matters. Allah, the Exalted, described them by defining them: "They do not fall short in corrupting you" — meaning they do not fall short in corrupting your religious and worldly affairs.

"They love your distress" — that is, they love your suffering and hardship; therefore they advise you only with what corrupts your affairs and causes you calamities and disasters in your life. And His saying, "Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater," is another description identifying these enemies whose adoption as confidants is forbidden, namely the appearance of hatred from their mouths in the words of disbelief and enmity toward Islam and its people that their tongues utter, and what they conceal of that in their breasts, which is greater than what slips from their tongues. Mighty and Majestic is He, further emphasizes His warning to the believers, saying: "We have already made the signs clear to you" — containing the explanation of your enemies, their conditions and their attributes, so that you may take heed — "if you use your reason." That is, the address and what is recited to you and said to you.

Then Allah, the Exalted, says, informing and warning: "There you are, O Muslims, loving them while they do not love you." Allah knew that among the believers there are those who love some of the disbelievers because of an apparent bond of kindness between them, so Allah, the Exalted, informed about these people, just as the mercy and compassion of the believer may extend even to his enemies. Therefore Allah mentioned this and informed of it, and it is the truth. He said: "And you believe in the Book, all of it" — that is, while they do not believe in your Book. So look at the difference between you and them; how then can you take them as intimate confidants to whom you confide your secrets?

Allah, the Exalted, informed about the hypocrites that when they meet the believers they say, "We believe," and when they are alone and withdraw among themselves, they recall them and become enraged at them, to the point of biting the tips of their fingers out of the intensity of rage. Allah, the Exalted, said: "And when they meet you they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage." Here He commanded His Messenger to invoke destruction upon them, saying to him: "Say, O Our Messenger, to them: 'Die in your rage; indeed Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts.'" Therefore He informed about them, uncovering what their souls harbor and conceal in their breasts.

This is what the first two verses [118] and [119] contain. As for the third verse [120], it also contains a description of the psychological state of the disbelievers, whose adoption as confidants is forbidden: their displeasure and pain at what they see of the good condition of the Muslims, such as their unity, the unity of their word, their victory, their honor, their strength and the abundance of their provision; and likewise their joy and delight at whatever disagreement among the Muslims they may witness, or a defeat befalling one of their armies, or a change in their condition that harms and does not please them. This is the extreme of enmity and the intensity of hatred. So would such people be taken as allies? Certainly not. Allah the Exalted said: "If good touches you, it distresses them; and if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it." When Allah, the Exalted, had described these disbelievers with frightening and terrifying attributes, He said, removing fear from His servants, the believers: "But if you are patient and mindful of Allah regarding His command and prohibition and His laws in His creation, their scheming will not harm you at all, because Allah is your Guardian, observing their movements and all their conduct, and He will nullify it all." This meaning is indicated by His saying in the concluding clause: "Indeed Allah is encompassing of what they do."

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of taking advisers and friends from among the people of disbelief in general, and the prohibition of disclosing to them the secrets of the Islamic state and the matters that Muslims conceal from their enemies, because of the great harm in that.

2- Explanation of the mercy of the believers and their superiority over the disbelievers.

3- Explanation of the psychology of the disbelievers and what they harbor of the will for evil and corruption toward the Muslims.

4- Protection from the scheming and plotting of the disbelievers lies in patience, steadfastness, not showing fear before the disbelievers, then fearing Allah, the Exalted, by establishing His religion, adhering to His law, relying upon Him, and taking up His laws regarding strength and victory.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 121–123:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-idh ghadawta (وإذ غدوت): That is, "and remember when you set out," and al-ghadw (الغدوّ, going out) means going forth at the beginning of the day.

Min ahlika (من أهلك): Ahl (أهل) a man's wife and children. Min here indicates the starting point, when the Prophet (ﷺ) left his house in the morning of Saturday for Uhud, where the polytheists had camped on Wednesday.

Tubawwi'u al-mu'minin (تبوّىء المؤمنين): settling the fighters in the places you saw as suitable for them to stop at on the battlefield.

Hammat (هَمَّتْ): she (the group) resolved within herself to return to Madinah, and her intention turned toward that.

Ta'ifatan (طائفتان): they are Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah from the Ansar.

Tafshalā (تفشلا): become weak and return to their homes, leaving the Messenger and those with him to fight the battle alone.

Wallahu waliyyuhuma (والله وليهما): the One who manages their affairs and supports them; for this reason He preserved them from abandoning the march to the battle.

Bi-Badr (ببدر): Badr is the name of a man, and the place was named after him because he had water there. It is now a village about one hundred and fifty miles (kilometres) from the City of the Prophet (Madinah).

Wa-antum adhillah (وأنتم أذلة): because your number and equipment were few, and the enemy was superior to you.

The meaning of the verses:

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 124–127:

Explanation of the words:

Alan yakfikum (ألن يكفيكم): The interrogative is a denial, meaning it denies that it would be insufficient. Yakfikum (يكفيكم) means it fills your need.

An yumiddakum (أن يمدكم): That is, with angels as helpers for you in fighting your enemies, who surpass you in number and equipment.

Al-malā'ika (الملائكة): Their singular is malak (ملاك), and they are honored servants of God, created from light, who do not disobey God in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded.

Balā (بلى): A particle of affirmation, meaning: yes, it would suffice you.

Min fawrihim hādhā (من فورهم هذا): That is, from their direction, at this very time.

Musawwimīn (مسومين): Marked with signs by which you will recognize them.

Illā bushrā lakum (إلا بشرى لكم): Bushrā (البشرى) is good news that brightens the face with cheer and joy.

Wa-litaṭma'inna bihi qulūbukum (ولتطمئن به قلوبكم): Tuma'nīnat al-qulūb (اطمئنان القلوب) is the calming of hearts and the removal of fear and anxiety from them.

Liyaqṭa'a ṭarafan (ليقطع طرفاً): Ṭaraf (الطرف) means a group; it means to destroy a group from the enemy's army.

Aw yakbitahum (أو يكبتهم): That is, to humiliate and disgrace them.

Fayanqalibū khā'ibīn (فينقلبوا خائبين): They return to their homes disappointed, not having achieved the victory they had hoped for.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to remind the Messenger ﷺ and the believers of the victory granted to them in the stand of patience and God-consciousness at Badr. He said: ﴿When you were saying to the believers﴾ when it reached them, while they were around the battle, that Kurz ibn Jabir al-Muharibi intended to supply the polytheists with his men to fight alongside them, and this grieved your companions, so you said: ﴿Would it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾ Balā: that is, it would suffice you. ﴿Yes, if you are patient and God-conscious, and they come upon you suddenly, from this very moment﴾ that is, from their direction and at this very time, ﴿your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked out﴾ with special signs and indications of their own. When Kurz was defeated before he moved and refrained from supplying Quraysh with fighters, God the Exalted did not reinforce His Messenger and the believers with the angels mentioned; He did not add to them beyond the first thousand with which He had reinforced them when they sought His help at the beginning of the battle. This is in Surat al-Anfal in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord and He answered you: I will reinforce you with a thousand angels﴾ [al-Anfal: 9]. That thousand is the one that actually descended and fought alongside the believers, and this was witnessed and known with certainty. As for the final promise of reinforcement, it was not fulfilled, because it was conditional on Kurz supplying Quraysh; when he did not supply them, God the Exalted did not supply the believers. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And God did not make it﴾ that is, the reinforcement mentioned ﴿except as glad tidings for you﴾ by which your hearts would be reassured and your souls would be calmed, so that the anxiety and agitation arising from fear of Kurz supplying the polytheists with fighters would disappear. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And victory is only from God, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. Al-'Azīz means the Overpowering; al-Ḥakīm is the One who places victory in its proper place, giving it to those deserving of it from among the patient and God-conscious. ﴿That He might cut off a group of those who disbelieved﴾ and this was done, and He destroyed seventy of the polytheists; ﴿or subdue them, so they turn back defeated﴾ that is, humiliate and disgrace them, for seventy of them were taken captive. ﴿So they return disappointed﴾ having not achieved the victory they had desired.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The explanation of the cause of the Muslims' defeat at Uhud, which was their lack of patience and their neglect of the principle of God-consciousness, when the archers disobeyed the command of the Messenger of God ﷺ and came down from the mountain, chasing the spoils. This is according to the interpretation that the promise of three thousand and of five thousand was at Uhud, and the promise was conditional upon patience and God-consciousness; when they were neither patient nor God-conscious, He did not reinforce them with the angels that had been mentioned to them.

2- Victory, although it has its factors such as large numbers and strength of equipment, is in the hand of God the Exalted. He may aid the weak and forsake the strong; therefore, it is obligatory to establish allegiance to God first, before preparing the numbers. Establishing this allegiance comes through faith, patience, and complete obedience to God and His Messenger, and then reliance upon God, Mighty and Majestic.

3- The establishment of the fighting of the angels alongside the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ at Badr as genuine fighting, for they descended in the form of men fighting on horses, with their distinguishing marks and signs upon them. Let no speaker say: one angel can defeat millions of men, so how is it conceivable that a thousand angels take part in fighting the polytheists when they were no more than a thousand men? God the Exalted sent them down in the form of men, so their appearance and strength became the strength of men. This is shown and witnessed by the fact that when the Angel of Death came to Moses in the form of a man wishing to take his soul, Moses, peace be upon him, struck him and gouged out his eye, and he returned to his Lord, exalted is He, and did not take the soul of Moses, peace be upon them both. From the narration of al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 124–127:

Explanation of the words:

Alan yakfikum (ألن يكفيكم): The interrogative is a denial, meaning it denies that it would be insufficient. Yakfikum (يكفيكم) means it fills your need.

An yumiddakum (أن يمدكم): That is, with angels as helpers for you in fighting your enemies, who surpass you in number and equipment.

Al-malā'ika (الملائكة): Their singular is malak (ملاك), and they are honored servants of God, created from light, who do not disobey God in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded.

Balā (بلى): A particle of affirmation, meaning: yes, it would suffice you.

Min fawrihim hādhā (من فورهم هذا): That is, from their direction, at this very time.

Musawwimīn (مسومين): Marked with signs by which you will recognize them.

Illā bushrā lakum (إلا بشرى لكم): Bushrā (البشرى) is good news that brightens the face with cheer and joy.

Wa-litaṭma'inna bihi qulūbukum (ولتطمئن به قلوبكم): Tuma'nīnat al-qulūb (اطمئنان القلوب) is the calming of hearts and the removal of fear and anxiety from them.

Liyaqṭa'a ṭarafan (ليقطع طرفاً): Ṭaraf (الطرف) means a group; it means to destroy a group from the enemy's army.

Aw yakbitahum (أو يكبتهم): That is, to humiliate and disgrace them.

Fayanqalibū khā'ibīn (فينقلبوا خائبين): They return to their homes disappointed, not having achieved the victory they had hoped for.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to remind the Messenger ﷺ and the believers of the victory granted to them in the stand of patience and God-consciousness at Badr. When Kurz was defeated before he moved and refrained from supplying Quraysh with fighters, God the Exalted did not reinforce His Messenger and the believers with the angels mentioned; He did not add to them beyond the first thousand with which He had reinforced them when they sought His help at the beginning of the battle. This is in Surat al-Anfal in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord and He answered you: I will reinforce you with a thousand angels﴾ [al-Anfal: 9]. That thousand is the one that actually descended and fought alongside the believers, and this was witnessed and known with certainty. As for the final promise of reinforcement, it was not fulfilled, because it was conditional on Kurz supplying Quraysh; when he did not supply them, God the Exalted did not supply the believers. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And God did not make it﴾ that is, the reinforcement mentioned ﴿except as glad tidings for you﴾ by which your hearts would be reassured and your souls would be calmed, so that the anxiety and agitation arising from fear of Kurz supplying the polytheists with fighters would disappear. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And victory is only from God, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. Al-'Azīz means the Overpowering; al-Ḥakīm is the One who places victory in its proper place, giving it to those deserving of it from among the patient and God-conscious. ﴿That He might cut off a group of those who disbelieved﴾ and this was done, and He destroyed seventy of the polytheists; ﴿or subdue them, so they turn back defeated﴾ that is, humiliate and disgrace them, for seventy of them were taken captive. ﴿So they return disappointed﴾ having not achieved the victory they had desired.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 128–132:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Amr (the matter): the affair; here it refers to God's accepting the repentance of the disbelievers or punishing them.

Shay' (a thing): an indefinite noun extremely vague in its reference. The root sense of shay' is: that which is known and can be reported.

Aw (or): here it means "until," i.e., "so be patient until He accepts their repentance or punishes them."

Lillahi ma fi as-samawati...: that is, He has dominion, creation, and servants; He disposes of them as He wills and judges as He desires.

La ta'kulun ar-riba (do not consume usury): there is no implication restricted to eating; rather every transaction involving riba is forbidden, whether it is eating, drinking, or wearing.

Ar-riba (usury): linguistically, increase. In the Sharia it is of two kinds: riba al-fadl (excess) and riba an-nasi'ah (deferment). Riba al-fadl occurs in gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates, and salt; when an item is sold for the same kind, both the excess (i.e., the increase) and the delay are forbidden. Riba an-nasi'ah is when a person owes a debt due at a certain term, the term arrives, he does not find the means to settle his debt, and he says to the creditor, "Postpone it for me and increase the debt."

Adafan mudaa'afah (multiplied manifold): there is no implication drawn from this, because it came in the form of what is usual; a single dirham of riba is forbidden just as a thousand is. In the Jahiliyyah they used to delay the debt and add increases in exchange for the delay until the debt multiplied into many times its amount.

Tuflihun (you prosper): you are saved from punishment and attain everlasting bliss in Paradise.

U'iddat lil-kafirin (prepared for the disbelievers): made ready and brought forth for those who deny Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

La'allakum turhamun (that you may receive mercy): so that you may be shown mercy and not be punished for the sin of disobedience that has proceeded from you.

Meaning of the verses:

It is established that the Prophet ﷺ had invoked punishment upon some individuals among the polytheists, and on the Day of Uhud, when his head was wounded and his front tooth broken, he said: "How can a people prosper who have done this to their prophet?" So Allah the Exalted revealed to him: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾, meaning: be patient until Allah accepts their repentance or punishes them for their wrongdoing, for they are wrongdoers. To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, in dominion, creation, and ownership; He disposes as He wills and judges as He desires. If He punishes, it is by His justice; if He shows mercy, it is by His grace. He is the Most Forgiving toward whoever repents, the Most Merciful toward whoever turns back.

This is what the first two verses [128] and [129] contain. As for the third verse [130], Allah the Exalted addressed His believing servants after they had left the Jahiliyyah and entered Islam, commanding them to abandon consuming riba and every dealing in it. He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: who have believed in Allah as Lord, in Islam as religion, and in Muhammad as Messenger, ﴿do not consume riba, multiplied manifold﴾. For a man would owe a debt, its term would come due, he would not find what to pay with, so he would go to his creditor and say, "Defer my debt and add to it for me," and so on for a second and third time, until the debt, which had been ten, becomes twenty or thirty. This is the meaning of His words "multiplied manifold." Then He commanded them to fear Him, the Mighty and Majestic, and promised them prosperity, saying: ﴿And fear Allah that you may prosper﴾, meaning: so that you may prosper by being saved from punishment and attaining reward, which is Paradise.

In the fourth verse [131], He commanded them to beware of the Fire prepared for the disbelievers, which is made ready and brought forth for them. Guarding against it is through obeying Allah and obeying His Messenger ﷺ. He said: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾, meaning those who deny Allah and His Messenger, and therefore do not act in obedience to them, since denial prevents obedience. In the last verse [132], He commanded them to obey Him and His Messenger and promised them mercy in this world and the Hereafter on account of that. It seems to allude to those who disobeyed the Messenger of Allah at Uhud, namely the archers who abandoned their defensive positions, which resulted in the believers suffering the worst defeat. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy﴾, meaning: so that He may show you mercy, accept your repentance, forgive you, and admit you into the Abode of Peace and everlasting bliss.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The Lord, the Exalted, alone holds sole command over all affairs; none of His creatures has any authority over anything except what He has permitted the servant.

2- Wrongdoing merits punishment, unless the Lord overtakes the servant with repentance, so he repents, and He forgives him and pardons him.

3- The absolute prohibition of consuming riba, whether multiplied or not.

4- A clarification of the riba of the Jahiliyyah, which is precisely what Allah the Exalted forbade in His words: ﴿do not consume riba﴾.

5- The obligation of taqwa (God-consciousness) for whoever wishes prosperity in this world and the Hereafter.

6- The obligation to guard against the Fire, even if only by giving half a date.

7- The obligation to obey Allah and His Messenger to obtain divine mercy, which is pardon, forgiveness, and entry into Paradise.

La ta'kulun ar-riba (do not consume usury): there is no implication restricted to eating; rather every transaction involving riba is forbidden, whether it is eating, drinking, or wearing.

Ar-riba (usury): linguistically, increase. In the Sharia it is of two kinds: riba al-fadl (excess) and riba an-nasi'ah (deferment). Riba al-fadl occurs in gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates, and salt; when an item is sold for the same kind, both the excess (i.e., the increase) and the delay are forbidden. Riba an-nasi'ah is when a person owes a debt due at a certain term, the term arrives, he does not find the means to settle his debt, and he says to the creditor, "Postpone it for me and increase the debt."

Adafan mudaa'afah (multiplied manifold): there is no implication drawn from this, because it came in the form of what is usual; a single dirham of riba is forbidden just as a thousand is. In the Jahiliyyah they used to delay the debt and add increases in exchange for the delay until the debt multiplied into many times its amount.

Tuflihun (you prosper): you are saved from punishment and attain everlasting bliss in Paradise.

U'iddat lil-kafirin (prepared for the disbelievers): made ready and brought forth for those who deny Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

La'allakum turhamun (that you may receive mercy): so that you may be shown mercy and not be punished for the sin of disobedience that has proceeded from you.

Meaning of the verses:

It is established that the Prophet ﷺ had invoked punishment upon some individuals among the polytheists, and on the Day of Uhud, when his head was wounded and his front tooth broken, he said: "How can a people prosper who have done this to their prophet?" So Allah the Exalted revealed to him: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾, meaning: be patient until Allah accepts their repentance or punishes them for their wrongdoing, for they are wrongdoers. To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, in dominion, creation, and ownership; He disposes as He wills and judges as He desires. If He punishes, it is by His justice; if He shows mercy, it is by His grace. He is the Most Forgiving toward whoever repents, the Most Merciful toward whoever turns back.

This is what the first two verses [128] and [129] contain. As for the third verse [130], Allah the Exalted addressed His believing servants after they had left the Jahiliyyah and entered Islam, commanding them to abandon consuming riba and every dealing in it. He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: who have believed in Allah as Lord, in Islam as religion, and in Muhammad as Messenger, ﴿do not consume riba, multiplied manifold﴾. For a man would owe a debt, its term would come due, he would not find what to pay with, so he would go to his creditor and say, "Defer my debt and add to it for me," and so on for a second and third time, until the debt, which had been ten, becomes twenty or thirty. This is the meaning of His words "multiplied manifold." Then He commanded them to fear Him, the Mighty and Majestic, and promised them prosperity, saying: ﴿And fear Allah that you may prosper﴾, meaning: so that you may prosper by being saved from punishment and attaining reward, which is Paradise.

In the fourth verse [131], He commanded them to beware of the Fire prepared for the disbelievers, which is made ready and brought forth for them. Guarding against it is through obeying Allah and obeying His Messenger ﷺ. He said: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾, meaning those who deny Allah and His Messenger, and therefore do not act in obedience to them, since denial prevents obedience. In the last verse [132], He commanded them to obey Him and His Messenger and promised them mercy in this world and the Hereafter on account of that. It seems to allude to those who disobeyed the Messenger of Allah at Uhud, namely the archers who abandoned their defensive positions, which resulted in the believers suffering the worst defeat. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy﴾, meaning: so that He may show you mercy, accept your repentance, forgive you, and admit you into the Abode of Peace and everlasting bliss.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The Lord, the Exalted, alone holds sole command over all affairs; none of His creatures has any authority over anything except what He has permitted the servant.

2- Wrongdoing merits punishment, unless the Lord overtakes the servant with repentance, so he repents, and He forgives him and pardons him.

3- The absolute prohibition of consuming riba, whether multiplied or not.

4- A clarification of the riba of the Jahiliyyah, which is precisely what Allah the Exalted forbade in His words: ﴿do not consume riba﴾.

5- The obligation of taqwa (God-consciousness) for whoever wishes prosperity in this world and the Hereafter.

6- The obligation to guard against the Fire, even if only by giving half a date.

7- The obligation to obey Allah and His Messenger to obtain divine mercy, which is pardon, forgiveness, and entry into Paradise.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 133–136:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-sari'u (and hasten): al-musara'ah (hastening) ilaa al-shay' means to hasten toward a thing and rush to it without slackness or delay.

Ila maghfiratin (to forgiveness): al-maghfirah (forgiveness) is the covering of sins and not calling one to account for them. What is meant here is hastening to repentance by abandoning sins, and increasing in seeking forgiveness. In the hadith: "No man commits a sin, then performs ablution, then prays, and then seeks forgiveness from Allah, except that He forgives him" (ﷺ). Wa-jannah (and Paradise): al-Jannah is the abode of bliss above the heavens, and hastening to it is by increasing in righteous deeds.

U'iddat (it has been prepared): huyyi'at (made ready) and brought into existence, so it now exists, prepared.

Lil-muttaqin (for the God-conscious): al-muttaqun are those who fear Allah, the Exalted, and so do not disobey Him by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act; and if a sin occurs from them, they repent from it immediately.

Fi al-sarra'i wa al-darra'i (in ease and in hardship): al-sarra' is the state that gladdens, which is ease and wealth; al-darra' is the state that harms, which is poverty.

Wa al-kazimina al-ghayz (and those who restrain anger): kazm al-ghayz is restraining it, and al-ghayz is a psychological pain that arises when a person is harmed in his body, honour or wealth. Restraining anger is not showing it through the limbs, by insult, beating or the like, for the sake of revenge or retaliation.

Wa al-'afina 'ani al-nas (and those who pardon people): al-'afw is not calling the wrongdoer to account while being able to do so.

Yuhibb al-muhsinin (Allah loves the good-doers): al-muhsinun are those who are dutiful and do not do evil in word or deed.

Fahishah (an abomination): al-fahishah is an ugly deed of extreme ugliness, such as adultery and major sins.

Aw zalamu anfusahum (or wrong themselves): by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act, thereby defiling themselves; this is wronging themselves.

Wa lam yusirru (and do not persist): i.e., they hasten to repentance, because iṣrar (persistence) is holding fast to a thing and binding oneself to it, derived from ṣirr (a bag tied shut), which is well known.

Wa hum ya'lamun (while they know): i.e., that they are opposing the Sharia by abandoning what it has made obligatory, or by doing what it has forbidden.

Wa ni'ma ajru al-'amilin (and excellent is the reward of the workers): which is Paradise.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, addressed the believers, forbidding them to consume riba (usury) and commanding them to be mindful of Him, the Mighty and Majestic, and to guard against the Fire, by abandoning riba and abandoning all other sins that bring about the punishment of Allah, and called them to obey Him and obey His Messenger, so that they might be shown mercy in their worldly life and in the Hereafter, He commanded them in the first verse [133] to hasten toward two things: the first, the forgiveness of their sins, by sincere repentance; and the second, entry into Paradise, which He described for them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-conscious﴾, meaning: it has been brought into existence and made ready for the God-conscious. Hastening to Paradise is hastening toward the causes of entering it, which are faith and righteous deeds, for by them the soul is purified and made good, so that it becomes fit to enter Paradise.

This is what the first verse contains. As for the second [134] and third [135] verses, they contain the attributes of the God-conscious for whom Paradise, the abode of peace, has been prepared. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship﴾ describes them as frequent spenders in the way of Allah, in all their circumstances, of wealth and poverty, hardship and ease. His saying: ﴿and those who restrain anger﴾ describes them with forbearance and generosity of soul. His saying: ﴿and those who pardon people﴾ describes them with forgiveness and overlooking the lapses of others out of nobility; and this action is clear good-doing, and from here they were given the good news of Allah's love for them, so He said, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers﴾, as an encouragement to good-doing and to persisting in it in word and deed. His saying: ﴿And those who, when they commit an abomination or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ describes them with constant remembrance of Allah and absence of heedlessness; so when they commit an abomination, a grave sin, or wrong themselves with a sin less than the abominable, they remember Allah's threat and His prohibition of what they did, and so they hasten to repentance, which is ceasing from the sin, regretting the deed, resolving not to return to it, and seeking Allah's forgiveness for it.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and do not persist in what they did while they know﴾ describes them with not persisting, meaning continuing in sin and not abandoning it, while they know that it is a sin resulting from their abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act. As for the fourth verse [136], it contains the explanation of their recompense for their faith and piety, and for the psychological perfections and spiritual purity with which they were characterised, namely the forgiveness of their sins, all their sins, and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The Bountiful, the Mighty and Majestic, praised what He recompensed them with, the forgiveness and eternal abiding in Paradise, the abode of lasting bliss, saying: ﴿and excellent is the reward of the workers﴾.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation of hastening repentance and not delaying it, by His saying: ﴿And hasten﴾.

2- The vastness of Paradise, and that it has already been created, by His saying: ﴿prepared﴾.

3- The God-conscious are the people of Paradise and its rightful heirs.

4- The virtue of continuous spending in the way of Allah, even if it is little.

5- The virtue of the trait of restraining anger, by not rushing to revenge and retaliation.

6- The virtue of pardoning people in general, believer and disbeliever, righteous and wicked.

7- The virtue of seeking forgiveness and abandoning persistence in disobedience, by the verse and by the hadith: "One who seeks forgiveness does not persist, even if he returns to the sin seventy times in a day." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud, and graded hasan by Ibn Kathir.

The Bountiful, the Mighty and Majestic, praised what He recompensed them with, the forgiveness and eternal abiding in Paradise, the abode of lasting bliss, saying: ﴿and excellent is the reward of the workers﴾.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation of hastening repentance and not delaying it, by His saying: ﴿And hasten﴾.

2- The vastness of Paradise, and that it has already been created, by His saying: ﴿prepared﴾.

3- The God-conscious are the people of Paradise and its rightful heirs.

4- The virtue of continuous spending in the way of Allah, even if it is little.

5- The virtue of the trait of restraining anger, by not rushing to revenge and retaliation.

6- The virtue of pardoning people in general, believer and disbeliever, righteous and wicked.

7- The virtue of seeking forgiveness and abandoning persistence in disobedience, by the verse and by the hadith: "One who seeks forgiveness does not persist, even if he returns to the sin seventy times in a day." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud, and graded hasan by Ibn Kathir.

Explanation of the words:

Qad khalat: khalat means "passed away" (madat).

Sunan: plural of sunnah (sunna), which is the course and manner upon which an individual or a community lives. The sunan of God Most High in His creation is His past law regarding creation.

Fasiru fi al-ard: the command is one of guidance, to stand upon the abodes of those who perished and passed away, so that you may take heed.

Aqibat al-mukadhdhibin: the final outcome of their affair, which is what befell them of destruction and ruin, like 'Ad and Thamud.

Hadha bayan lil-nas: that is, what is mentioned in the verses is a clarification for mankind, by which they distinguish guidance from error, and what accompanies them of success and loss.

Mawi'zah: admonition, the state by which the believer is admonished and so takes the path of salvation.

Wa la tahinu: do not be weak (la tad'ifu).

Qarh: qarh means the trace of a weapon on the body, like a wound; with a dammed qaf (qurh) it means pain.

Al-ayyam: plural of yawm, along with the nights; what is meant is what God causes to occur of the vicissitudes of life, of good and other, of honour and humiliation.

Shuhada': plural of shahid, which is one killed in the way of God, and also a witness, one who bears witness over others.

Liyumahhisa: so that He may purify the believers from the stains of transgressions and the filth of sins.

Yamhaq: He erases and removes the traces of disbelief and the disbelievers.

Meaning of the verses:

When what happened happened of the defeat of the believers due to their lack of patience and the obedience required of leadership, God Most High mentioned those events together with their understanding, so that they would remain guidance and admonition for the God-fearing among the believers, and He began with His words: ﴿Indeed, there have passed before you precedents; so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ He informed the believers that His sunan had passed concerning those before them from the nations, such as the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and others. God Most High sent His messengers to them, and they denied them, so God executed His sunan upon them, destroying the deniers and saving the believers after what they suffered from the harm of their denying peoples. His sunan will proceed today in the same way: He will save you, give you victory, and destroy your enemies who deny. And if you doubt, then travel through the earth, stand upon the traces of the perished, and observe how their end was. Then God said: what I have mentioned in these verses is a clarification for mankind, by which they distinguish truth from falsehood and guidance from error, and a guidance by which they are guided to the path of peace, and an admonition by which the God-fearing are admonished, being prepared through their faith and piety to take heed, so they obey God and His Messenger and are saved and succeed. This is what the first two verses [137] and [138] contained. As for the third verse [139] and the fourth [140], they contained the consolation of the Lord, Most High, to the believers for what befell them on the day of Uhud, when He said addressing them: ﴿And do not weaken﴾, that is, do not be feeble so that you sit back from jihad and action, and do not grieve over what you lost of your men, and you will be the superior ones, that is, the victors over your enemies, prevailing over them; and that applies to what has passed and what is yet to come, on condition of your faith and piety. Know that if a wound (qarh) touches you through death or injuries, it should not be that this weakens you or holds you back from continuing jihad, for your enemy has likewise been touched by a wound like it, at the battle of Badr. War is alternating: a day for you and a day against you, and this is one of the sunan of your Lord in life. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And these days We alternate among the people.﴾ Then, after this noble and wise consolation, God mentioned to them the cause of this grave event and its secret, and said: ﴿And that God may know those who believe and take from among you martyrs﴾, that is, so that through this painful event the faith of the believers would become manifest. Indeed, the hypocrites turned back from the road under the leadership of their chief, the greatest hypocrite, 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, while the believers continued their march and fought their battle, so their faith became manifest, and God took martyrs from among them. They numbered about seventy martyrs, among them four from the Muhajirun, headed by Hamza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr; the rest were from the Ansar, may God be pleased with them all.

And His words: ﴿And that God may purify those who believe﴾, that is, He brought about what He brought about at Uhud of struggle and defeat, to purify the believers from their sins and cleanse them so that they become completely pure, and to erase the disbelievers by destroying them and ending their existence.

This lesson benefited the believers afterward, so they did not depart from obedience to their Prophet, and by that their victories continued until they removed the breath of disbelief and the disbelievers from the whole land of the Arabian Peninsula.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 142–145:

Explanation of the words:

Am hasibtum (أم حسبتم): Rather, did you suppose? You should not suppose this supposition. The interrogative is one of denial.

Wa lamma ya'lam (ولما يعلم): And He has not tested you through jihad until He knows, with the knowledge of manifestation, who among you strives and who does not, as He already knows it in the hidden depths of the matter and its secrets.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 146–148:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa ka-ayyin min nabiyyin*: Many of the prophets. Some say *ka-ayyin* is read as *kam* (how many), and in that case it denotes multiplicity.

*Ribbiyyun*: *rabbaniyyun* (devoted to the Lord), scholars, righteous people, pious people, and worshippers.

*Fa-ma wahanu li-ma asabahum*: They did not weaken in fighting, nor were they routed because of what befell them of killing and wounds.

*Wa-ma istakanu*: They did not submit or humble themselves before their enemy.

*Al-israf* (excess): Going beyond the limit in matters that have limits at which one ought to stop.

*Fa-ataahumu-llah thawab al-dunya*: Allah the Exalted gave them the reward of this world, namely victory and spoils of war.

*Al-muhsinin* (the good-doers): Those who make their intentions good, so they sincerely dedicate their deeds to Allah, and who make their deeds good, so they perform them in accordance with what was prescribed regarding their manner, number and times.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues about the events of the Battle of Uhud. Here the Exalted mentions what completes His rebuke of the believers in the preceding verses for their lack of patience, their defeat, and their abandonment of their Prophet alone in the middle of the battle, until he called out to them: "Come to me, servants of Allah! Come to me, servants of Allah!" and some men returned to him. Allah the Exalted then said, informing them of what would serve as an admonition and lesson for them: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, and with him fought many devoted scholars and pious, righteous people; so they did not weaken, i.e., they did not grow feeble, nor did they humble themselves to their enemy, nor submit to him, as some of you, O believers, intended to do; rather they endured in fighting alongside their prophets, bearing the pains of killing and wounding. Therefore their Lord, the Exalted, loved them for that, for Allah loves the patient.﴾

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 149–151:

Explanation of the words:

*In tuti'u alladhina kafaru*: What is meant by obeying the disbelievers is accepting their words and following their guidance.

*Yaruddukum ala a'qabikum*: They will cause you to return to disbelief after faith.

*Khasirin* (losers): deprived of every good in this world, and of your own selves and your families on the Day of Resurrection.

*Bal Allahu mawlakum* (But Allah is your Protector): Rather, obey Allah, your Lord, your Guardian and your Master, for He is the best to be obeyed and the most worthy to be obeyed.

*Al-Ru'b* (terror): intense fear arising from anticipating defeat and harm.

*Ma'wahum* (their abode): the place where they lodge and stay.

*Mathwa* (dwelling place): the mathwa is the place of thawa, which means residing and settling.

*Al-zalimin* (the wrongdoers): the polytheists who obeyed other than Allah, the Exalted, and worshipped other than Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the events of the Battle of Uhud. It is narrated that when some of the hypocrites saw the defeat of the believers at Uhud, they said concerning the believers: "Return to your religion and your brothers; if Muhammad were a prophet, he would not have been killed," and so on, of the kinds of suggestions that might be made in that difficult hour, which this divine address to the believers has exposed, warning them against obeying the disbelievers, in His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will return you to your heels, and you will turn about as losers﴾. There is no doubt that the disbelievers demanded that the believers obey them by carrying out some suggestions whose outward appearance is advice but whose inner reality is deceit and trickery. So Allah, the Exalted, forbade them to obey them in that. This prohibition, although it was revealed concerning a particular situation, is general for the Muslims throughout all time: it is not lawful to obey the disbelievers, whether from the People of the Book or others, in anything they command or suggest. Whoever obeys them, they will turn him back from his religion to theirs, and so he turns back (*yanqalib*: returns) as a loser in his worldly life and his Hereafter, and we seek refuge in Allah. This is what the first verse [149] contains. As for the second verse [150], it contains the command to obey Him, the Exalted, since He is more deserving of that, for He is their Lord, their Guardian and their Master, so He is more worthy of their obedience than the disbelievers. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Master﴾, so obey Him and do not obey His enemies. And if you wish to seek victory by obeying the disbelievers, then Allah, the Exalted, is the best of helpers; so seek victory from Him by obeying Him, for He will give you victory. In the third verse [151], when the believers complied with the command of their Lord and did not obey the disbelievers, their Lord, glorified and exalted be He, promised them that He would cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers, which is fear, dread and panic, so that you may be able to fight them and overcome them, and that is the victory you desire. Exalted is He, He gave the reason for this action toward the disbelievers: they associated with Him deities whom they worshipped alongside Him, for which He had sent down no authority or sanction. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾. Finally, their abode is the Fire, that is, the place of their residence is the Fire, and Allah, the Exalted, condemned residing in the Fire, saying: "and their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the dwelling of the wrongdoers," meaning: the Fire is a wretched place to stay for the wrongdoers, who are the polytheists.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Obeying the disbelievers is forbidden when one has a choice.

2- Explanation of the secret behind the prohibition of obeying the disbelievers: it results in apostasy, and we seek refuge in Allah.

3- Explanation of the rule: whoever seeks victory from other than Allah, Allah humiliates him.

4- Allah promised the believers victory after casting terror into the hearts of their enemies. Abu Sufyan intended to return to Medina after his withdrawal from Uhud, to finish off the men who remained in Medina, as his soul had enticed him to do; then Allah cast terror into his heart, so he turned away from the plan by Allah's arrangement.

5- The invalidity of every claim for which its holders have no proof, which is what is referred to as *sultan* (authority) in the verse, since by proof the truth is established and its holder attains it through it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 152–153:

Explanation of the words:

ṣadaqakumu-llāhu waʿdahu (صدقكم الله وعده): He fulfilled for you what He promised through His Messenger, when he said to the archers, "Hold your positions, for we will not cease to be victorious as long as you remain in your positions."

taḥussūnahum (تحسونهم): You kill them, for ḥass (الحس) means killing; one says ḥassahu when he killed him, thus annulling his sense (ḥass).

bi-idhnihi (بإذنه): by His permission for you to fight them, and by His help to you in that.

fashiltum (فشلتم): you became weak and cowardly in fighting.

tuṣʿidūna (تصعدون): you flee across the land, fleeing from the battle; one says aṣʿada when he went off into the high ground (ṣaʿīd al-arḍ).

wa-lā talwūna ʿalā aḥad (ولا تلوون على أحد): you do not turn your heads toward anyone to look at them.

wa-r-rasūlu yadʿūkum fī ukhrākum (والرسول يدعوكم في أخراكم): that is, he calls you from behind you: "To me, servants of God! Return to me, servants of God! Return to me!"

fa-athābakum ghamman bi-ghamm (فأثابكم غما بغم): He repaid you for your disobedience and your flight with grief upon grief. Al-ghamm is pain of the soul and constriction of the chest.

mā fātakum (ما فاتكم): of the spoils of war.

wa-lā mā aṣābakum (ولا ما أصابكم): of death, wounds, pains and hardships.

The meaning of the verses:

The context is still about the events of Uhud. Earlier in the context, Allah the Exalted forbade the believers from obeying the disbelievers in whatever they suggest and counsel. He promised them that He would cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers, and He did — praise be to Him — when Abu Sufyan resolved to return to Madina to kill whoever was in it and uproot them, so Allah cast terror into his heart and the hearts of his followers, and they changed course from attacking Madina a second time and went back to Makkah. The Messenger and the believers returned from Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad without meeting Abu Sufyan and his army. In these two verses, Allah the Exalted informs them of His favour upon them, in that He fulfilled for them what He had promised of victory. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾.

This was because the Messenger ﷺ, when he stationed the archers in their positions — and they were thirty archers — and appointed over them ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr, commanded them not to leave their positions whatever the situation, and said to them: "We will not cease to be victorious as long as you remain in your positions, shooting at the enemy, thereby protecting our backs." Indeed the battle raged, and Allah fulfilled His promise to them: the polytheists fled before them, leaving everything behind and fleeing with their lives, while the believers were killing them (yuḥassūnahum, i.e., killing them outright) by Allah's permission and His support. When the archers saw the defeat of the polytheists and the believers gathering the spoils, they said: "What is the point of our staying here while the people are taking booty? Come, let us go down to the battlefield to take spoils." Their commander ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr reminded them of the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but they interpreted it otherwise, descended to the battlefield seeking the spoils. Khālid ibn al-Walīd was in command of the polytheists' cavalry, and when he saw that the archers had vacated their positions except for a few, he charged with his horsemen against them, took their positions and killed those who remained there, and shot at the Muslims from behind, so they were thrown into disarray. The polytheists then returned to them and clashed between the resentful archers and the fiercely fighting warriors, and the calamity befell them: seventy of the believers were killed, among them Ḥamza, the uncle of the Messenger ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was wounded in his face and his front tooth was broken, and Satan cried out that Muḥammad had been killed, and the believers fled from the battlefield except for a few. Concerning this Allah the Exalted says: ﴿until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter﴾, meaning the archers' dispute with their commander ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr, when he forbade them to abandon their positions and reminded them of the command of the Messenger; they disputed with him over its understanding, opposed the order and descended. This happened after they saw their brothers victorious and their enemies defeated. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and you disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾, that is, of victory, ﴿among you are those who desire this world﴾, those who descended to the field to gather the spoils, ﴿and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾, who are ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr and those who stood firm with him in their positions until they were martyred there. His words ﴿Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾ report the abandonment of fighting because of the weakness that befell them when they saw themselves trapped between the polytheist archers and their warriors, so they fled up into the valley saving themselves. This occurred by Allah's knowledge and decree, and its wisdom is indicated by His words ﴿to test you﴾, that is, to examine you, so that He may see the sincere believer distinguished from the hypocritical liar, and the patient from the one who despairs. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿when you were climbing away﴾, meaning: He pardoned you at the time you fled climbing up the valleys, fleeing from the battle, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you, "To me, servants of God! taḥussūnahum (تحسونهم): You kill them, for ḥass (الحس) means killing; one says ḥassahu when he killed him, thus annulling his sense (ḥass).

bi-idhnihi (بإذنه): by His permission for you to fight them, and by His help to you in that.

fashiltum (فشلتم): you became weak and cowardly in fighting.

tuṣʿidūna (تصعدون): you flee across the land, fleeing from the battle; one says aṣʿada when he went off into the high ground (ṣaʿīd al-arḍ).

wa-lā talwūna ʿalā aḥad (ولا تلوون على أحد): you do not turn your heads toward anyone to look at them.

wa-r-rasūlu yadʿūkum fī ukhrākum (والرسول يدعوكم في أخراكم): that is, he calls you from behind you: "To me, servants of God! Return to me, servants of God! Return to me!"

fa-athābakum ghamman bi-ghamm (فأثابكم غما بغم): He repaid you for your disobedience and your flight with grief upon grief. Al-ghamm is pain of the soul and constriction of the chest.

The Messenger and the believers returned from Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad without meeting Abu Sufyan and his army. In these two verses, Allah the Exalted informs them of His favour upon them, in that He fulfilled for them what He had promised of victory. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾.

This was because the Messenger ﷺ, when he stationed the archers in their positions — and they were thirty archers — and appointed over them ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr, commanded them not to leave their positions whatever the situation, and said to them: "We will not cease to be victorious as long as you remain in your positions, shooting at the enemy, thereby protecting our backs." When the archers saw the defeat of the polytheists and the believers gathering the spoils, they said: "What is the point of our staying here while the people are taking booty? Come, let us go down to the battlefield to take spoils." Their commander ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr reminded them of the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but they interpreted it otherwise, descended to the battlefield seeking the spoils. Khālid ibn al-Walīd was in command of the polytheists' cavalry, and when he saw that the archers had vacated their positions except for a few, he charged with his horsemen against them, took their positions and killed those who remained there, and shot at the Muslims from behind, so they were thrown into disarray. This happened after they saw their brothers victorious and their enemies defeated. Return!", and you were fleeing without turning toward anyone, that is, without looking at him. His words ﴿So He repaid you with grief upon grief﴾ mean He repaid you for your disobedience with grief. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 154–155:

Explanation of the words:

Amanah nu'asan (security, drowsiness): Amanah means security, and nu'as (drowsiness) is a relaxation that comes over the body before sleep.

Yaghshā ṭā'ifatan minkum (it overtook a group of you): it befell the believers so that they could rest, and it did not befall the hypocrites.

Ahammathum anfusuhum (they were concerned only for themselves): that is, they thought only of saving themselves, indifferent to what had befallen the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions.

Ẓann al-jāhiliyyah (the ignorant notion, the ignorance-born opinion): this is their belief that the Prophet had been killed, or that he would not be helped.

Hal lanā min al-amr (do we have any say in the matter?): that is, we have no share in the matter at all.

Mā lā yubdūna laka (what they do not reveal to you): that is, what they do not show you.

Labarza alladhīna (those destined would have gone out): would have come out of Madinah openly to meet their fates there.

Kutiba 'alayhimu al-qatl (death was decreed for them): this refers to what was written in the book of decrees, namely the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-maḥfūẓ).

Maḍāji'ihim (their resting places): plural of maḍja', which is the place of sleep and lying down; here it means the place where they were struck down and killed.

Liyabtali (to test): to try.

Waliyumaḥḥiṣa (to purify): tamḥīṣ means distinguishing, that is, making one thing manifest from another, like the manifestation of faith from hypocrisy, and love from hatred.

Istazallahumu al-shayṭān (Satan caused them to slip): he led them into error, which is a sin; and it was the fleeing from jihad.

The meaning of the two verses:

The context continues to speak of the Battle of Uhud. In the first verse [154], Allah, exalted is He, informs of great matters. The first is that, after the grief that befell the believers, He sent down complete security upon the people of certainty specifically, so fear departed from them, to the extent that one of them would sleep while holding his sword, so it would fall from his hand, and then he would pick it up again. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then He sent down upon you, after the grief, security, drowsiness overtaking a group of you﴾. The second is that Allah deprived the people of doubt and hypocrisy of that security, so fear continued to tear at their hearts and grief dominated their souls, and they thought only of themselves, how they might escape death; they are the ones referred to in His saying, ﴿and a group who were concerned only for themselves﴾. The third is that Allah exposed their inner secrets, saying: they think about Allah other than the truth, the ignorant notion. What is meant by their thinking about Allah other than the truth is the notion of the polytheists, who believed that Islam was false, that Muhammad was not a Messenger, that the believers would be defeated and killed, and that Islam and those who call to it would come to an end. The fourth is that Allah exposed their secret, saying concerning them: ﴿They say, "Do we have any say in the matter?"﴾. They said this privately among themselves, and its meaning is: we have no say in the matter at all; had we had any, we would not have gone out, nor fought, nor would what has befallen us have befallen us. So Allah informed His Messenger of their secret and said to him: Answer them with your words: indeed the whole matter belongs to Allah. Then Allah, exalted is He, tore away their cover once more and exposed their secret, saying: ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you﴾, that is, they conceal within themselves disbelief, hatred and enmity toward you and your Companions, which they do not show you. The fifth is that when the hypocrites spoke privately and said: "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been slain here", they meant: if the matter were in their hands, they would not have gone out to fight the polytheists, because they are their brothers in polytheism and disbelief, nor would they have been killed with those who were killed at Uhud. So Allah commanded His Messenger to answer them by saying: ﴿Say: Even if you had remained in your houses, those destined for death would have come out to their resting places﴾, that is, those for whom death was decreed would have appeared and been struck down and died there, because what Allah has decreed is binding in every case, and there is no escaping destiny.

It was necessary that your going out to Uhud occur by the arrangement of Allah, "that Allah may test what is in your breasts," that is, He may examine what is in your hearts and distinguish what is within your hearts, so that what was hidden, which none knows but Him, becomes manifest to the realm of witnessing, that He and His Messenger and the believers may see it in its reality. This is due to Allah's knowledge of what the breasts contain. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Say: "Even if you had remained in your houses, those destined for death would have come out to their resting places. And that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts; and Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts."﴾

This is what the first verse contains. As for the second verse [155], it contains Allah's report of one fact that ought to be known: that those who turned away from the battle when the fighting intensified and the distress grew great, it was Satan who caused them to slip into this lapse, which is turning away from fighting because of some sins they had committed. Therefore Allah pardoned them and did not hold them accountable for this lapse. This is because Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing; He gives respite to His servant until he repents, and then He accepts his repentance and forgives him. Had He not been Forbearing, He would have held him accountable for the first sin and slip, and no one could have repented or been saved. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away﴾, that is, from the fighting, ﴿on the day the two hosts met﴾, that is, the host of the believers and the host of the disbelievers at Uhud. ﴿It was only that Satan caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. And Allah has already pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

Guidance from the two verses:

1- Allah's honouring of His friends through the security He sent down into their hearts.

2- Allah's humiliating of His enemies by depriving them of what He honoured His friends with, while they were in one place.

3- Affirmation of the principle of qadar (divine decree), and that whoever has death written for him in a place will certainly die there.

4- The acts of Allah are never free of lofty wisdom, so it is obligatory to submit to Allah and be content with His acts in His creation.

5- Sin begets sin, and an evil deed gives rise to another evil deed; therefore repentance from sin is obligatory immediately.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 3, verses 156–158:

Explanation of the words:

"Amanu" (believed): they were truthful to God and His Messenger regarding what they reported of promise and threat.

"Ikhwanahum" (their brethren): this is the brotherhood of creed, not of lineage, and here it is the brotherhood of hypocrisy.

"Darabu fi al-ard" (they journeyed in the land): they traveled on foot in the land, going mostly for trade.

"Ghuzza" (raiders): plural of ghazin, meaning one who goes out to fight or to engage in similar matters of war.

"Al-hasrah" (regret): a pain that grips the soul because of the loss of something desired or the deprivation of something loved.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the events of the Battle of Uhud and its various outcomes. In this verse [156], God calls out to the believers who are sincere in their faith in God and His Messenger and in the promise and threat of God, calling them to forbid themselves from taking on the psychological characteristics of the disbelievers. Among these is the saying of the disbelievers to their brethren in disbelief when they journey in the land for trade or for raiding, and some of them die or some of them are killed by the decree and destiny of God: "Had they been with us, they would not have died, nor would they have been killed." This indicates the psychology of ignorance and the sickness of disbelief. By the custom of God, this statement of theirs produces for them, by His permission, psychological distress and heart-rending regrets that tear them apart and may even cost them their lives. Those disbelieving ignorant ones did not realize that God gives life and causes death; neither travel nor fighting causes death, and neither sitting at home out of cowardice and weakness brings life. This is the meaning of His words in this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said of their brothers when they traveled in the land or were raiders, "If they had remained with us, they would not have died or been killed." [They said this] so that God may make that a regret in their hearts. And God gives life and causes death, and God is Seeing of what you do.﴾ His words at the end of this verse, ﴿And God is Seeing of what you do﴾, contain a promise to the believers that if they desist from what He has forbidden them in the verse, and a threat if they do not desist: He will reward the good with good, and the evil with evil unless He pardons it.

As for the second verse [157], God gives glad tidings to His believing servants, informing them that if they are killed in the way of God or die in it, He will forgive them and have mercy on them, and that this is better than what the disbelievers gather of the goods of this world, that gathering of goods which made them cowardly about fighting and going out in the way of God. He said: ﴿And if you are killed in the cause of God or die, forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what they accumulate.﴾

In the third verse [158], He affirms that superiority contained in the previous verse, saying: ﴿And if you die or are killed﴾ in Our way ﴿—to God you will surely be gathered﴾ without doubt, and then your reward for your martyrdom and death in Our way will be fulfilled for you; and how excellent is what you are recompensed with in His gracious neighborhood.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The prohibition of resembling the disbelievers, outwardly and inwardly.

2- Regret begets griefs, and sorrow is a great distress and anguish; the believer repels this by remembering the decree and destiny, so he does not grieve over what has escaped him nor rejoice in what has been given to him of the goods of this world.

3- A death in the way of God is better than the world and what is in it.
